Those belong in the structural diagram. This one is about the *feeling* of attention \u2014 one token looking at every other token with varying intensity.\n\nThese are starting points, not ceilings. For the water heater: add a thermostat slider, animate the convection current, toggle heating vs standby. For the attention diagram: let the user click any token to become the query, scrub through layers, animate the weights settling. The goal is always to *show* how the thing works, not just *label* it.\n\n\n## UI components\n\n### Layout width\nThe widget container is 680px wide. Use `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(160px, 1fr))` for responsive columns \u2014 auto-fit lets the grid pick column count by available width.\n\n### Aesthetic\nFlat, clean, white surfaces. Minimal 0.5px borders. Generous whitespace. No gradients, no shadows (except functional focus rings). Everything should feel native to claude.ai \u2014 like it belongs on the page, not embedded from somewhere else.\n\n### Tokens\n- Borders: always `0.5px solid var(--color-border-tertiary)` (or `-secondary` for emphasis)\n- Corner radius: `var(--border-radius-md)` for most elements, `var(--border-radius-lg)` for cards\n- Cards: white bg (`var(--color-background-primary)`), 0.5px border, radius-lg, padding 1rem 1.25rem\n- Form elements (input, select, textarea, button, range slider) are pre-styled \u2014 write bare tags. Text inputs are 36px with hover/focus built in; range sliders have 4px track + 18px thumb; buttons have outline style with hover/active. Only add inline styles to override (e.g., different width).\n- Buttons: pre-styled with transparent bg, 0.5px border-secondary, hover bg-secondary, active scale(0.98). If it triggers sendPrompt, append a \u2197 arrow.\n- **Round every displayed number.** JS float math leaks artifacts \u2014 `0.1 + 0.2` gives `0.30000000000000004`, `7 * 1.1` gives `7.700000000000001`. Any number that reaches the screen (slider readouts, stat card values, axis labels, data-point labels, tooltips, computed totals) must go through `Math.round()`, `.toFixed(n)`, or `Intl.NumberFormat`. Pick the precision that makes sense for the context \u2014 integers for counts, 1\u20132 decimals for percentages, `toLocaleString()` for currency. For range sliders, also set `step=\"1\"` (or step=\"0.1\" etc.) so the input itself emits round values.\n- Spacing: use rem for vertical rhythm (1rem, 1.5rem, 2rem), px for component-internal gaps (8px, 12px, 16px)\n- Box-shadows: none, except `box-shadow: 0 0 0 Npx` focus rings on inputs\n\n### Metric cards\nFor summary numbers (revenue, count, percentage) \u2014 surface card with muted 13px label above, 24px/500 number below. `background: var(--color-background-secondary)`, no border, `border-radius: var(--border-radius-md)`, padding 1rem. Use in grids of 2-4 with `gap: 12px`. Distinct from raised cards (which have white bg + border).\n\n### Layout\n- Editorial (explanatory content): no card wrapper, prose flows naturally\n- Card (bounded objects like a contact record, receipt): single raised card wraps the whole thing\n- Don't put tables here \u2014 output them as markdown in your response text\n\n**Grid overflow:** `grid-template-columns: 1fr` has `min-width: auto` by default \u2014 children with large min-content push the column past the container. Use `minmax(0, 1fr)` to clamp.\n\n**Table overflow:** Tables with many columns auto-expand past `width: 100%` if cell contents exceed it. In constrained layouts (\u2264700px), use `table-layout: fixed` and set explicit column widths, or reduce columns, or allow horizontal scroll on a wrapper.\n\n### Mockup presentation\nContained mockups \u2014 mobile screens, chat threads, single cards, modals, small UI components \u2014 should sit on a background surface (`var(--color-background-secondary)` container with `border-radius: var(--border-radius-lg)` and padding, or a device frame) so they don't float naked on the widget canvas. Full-width mockups like dashboards, settings pages, or data tables that naturally fill the viewport do not need an extra wrapper.\n\n### 1. Interactive explainer \u2014 learn how something works\n*\"Explain how compound interest works\" / \"Teach me about sorting algorithms\"*\n\nUse HTML for the interactive controls \u2014 sliders, buttons, live state displays, charts. Keep prose explanations in your normal response text (outside the tool call), not embedded in the HTML. No card wrapper. Whitespace is the container.\n\n```html\n<div style=\"display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; margin: 0 0 1.5rem;\">\n  <label style=\"font-size: 14px; color: var(--color-text-secondary);\">Years</label>\n  <input type=\"range\" min=\"1\" max=\"40\" value=\"20\" id=\"years\" style=\"flex: 1;\" />\n  <span style=\"font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; min-width: 24px;\" id=\"years-out\">20</span>\n</div>\n\n<div style=\"display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; margin: 0 0 1.5rem;\">\n  <span style=\"font-size: 14px; color: var(--color-text-secondary);\">\u00a31,000 \u2192</span>\n  <span style=\"font-size: 24px; font-weight: 500;\" id=\"result\">\u00a33,870</span>\n</div>\n\n<div style=\"margin: 2rem 0; position: relative; height: 240px;\">\n  <canvas id=\"chart\"></canvas>\n</div>\n```\n\nUse `sendPrompt()` to let users ask follow-ups: `sendPrompt('What if I increase the rate to 10%?')`\n\n### 2. Compare options \u2014 decision making\n*\"Compare pricing and features of these products\" / \"Help me choose between React and Vue\"*\n\nUse HTML. Side-by-side card grid for options. Highlight differences with semantic colors. Interactive elements for filtering or weighting.\n\n- Each option in a card. Use badges for key differentiators.\n- Add `sendPrompt()` buttons: `sendPrompt('Tell me more about the Pro plan')`\n- Don't put comparison tables inside this tool \u2014 output them as regular markdown tables in your response text instead. The tool is for the visual card grid only.\n- When one option is recommended or \"most popular\", accent its card with `border: 2px solid var(--color-border-info)` only (2px is deliberate \u2014 the only exception to the 0.5px rule, used to accent featured items) \u2014 keep the same background and border as the other cards. Add a small badge (e.g. \"Most popular\") above or inside the card header using `background: var(--color-background-info); color: var(--color-text-info); font-size: 12px; padding: 4px 12px; border-radius: var(--border-radius-md)`.\n\n### 3. Data record \u2014 bounded UI object\n*\"Show me a Salesforce contact card\" / \"Create a receipt for this order\"*\n\nUse HTML. Wrap the entire thing in a single raised card. All content is sans-serif since it's pure UI. Use an avatar/initials circle for people (see example below).\n\n```html\n<div style=\"background: var(--color-background-primary); border-radius: var(--border-radius-lg); border: 0.5px solid var(--color-border-tertiary); padding: 1rem 1.25rem;\">\n  <div style=\"display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; margin-bottom: 16px;\">\n    <div style=\"width: 44px; height: 44px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--color-background-info); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-weight: 500; font-size: 14px; color: var(--color-text-info);\">MR</div>\n    <div>\n      <p style=\"font-weight: 500; font-size: 15px; margin: 0;\">Maya Rodriguez</p>\n      <p style=\"font-size: 13px; color: var(--color-text-secondary); margin: 0;\">VP of Engineering</p>\n    </div>\n  </div>\n  <div style=\"border-top: 0.5px solid var(--color-border-tertiary); padding-top: 12px;\">\n    <table style=\"width: 100%; font-size: 13px;\">\n      <tr><td style=\"color: var(--color-text-secondary); padding: 4px 0;\">Email</td><td style=\"text-align: right; padding: 4px 0; color: var(--color-text-info);\">m.rodriguez@acme.com</td></tr>\n      <tr><td style=\"color: var(--color-text-secondary); padding: 4px 0;\">Phone</td><td style=\"text-align: right; padding: 4px 0;\">+1 (415) 555-0172</td></tr>\n    </table>\n  </div>\n</div>\n```\n\n\n\n## Charts (Chart.js)\n```html\n<div style=\"position: relative; width: 100%; height: 300px;\">\n  <canvas id=\"myChart\" role=\"img\" aria-label=\"Bar chart of quarterly revenue, Q1 through Q4\">Quarterly revenue: Q1 12, Q2 19, Q3 8, Q4 15.</canvas>\n</div>\n<script src=\"https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/Chart.js/4.4.1/chart.umd.js\"></script>\n<script>\n  new Chart(document.getElementById('myChart'), {\n    type: 'bar',\n    data: { labels: ['Q1','Q2','Q3','Q4'], datasets: [{ label: 'Revenue', data: [12,19,8,15] }] },\n    options: { responsive: true, maintainAspectRatio: false }\n  });\n</script>\n```\n\n**Chart.js rules**:\n- Every `<canvas>` MUST have `role=\"img\"` and a descriptive `aria-label` summarizing what the chart shows, plus fallback text between the tags. Without these the chart is invisible to screen readers.\n- Never rely on color alone to distinguish data series. Pair each color with a secondary visual cue \u2014 dash pattern for lines, marker shape for scatter, fill pattern/hatching for bars and pie slices \u2014 and show both color and cue in the legend.\n- Canvas cannot resolve CSS variables. Use hardcoded hex or Chart.js defaults.\n- Wrap `<canvas>` in `<div>` with explicit `height` and `position: relative`.\n- **Canvas sizing**: set height ONLY on the wrapper div, never on the canvas element itself. Use position: relative on the wrapper and responsive: true, maintainAspectRatio: false in Chart.js options. Never set CSS height directly on canvas \u2014 this causes wrong dimensions, especially for horizontal bar charts.\n- For horizontal bar charts: wrapper div height should be at least (number_of_bars * 40) + 80 pixels.\n- Load UMD build via `<script src=\"https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...\">` \u2014 sets `window.Chart` global. Follow with plain `<script>` (no `type=\"module\"`).\n- Multiple charts: use unique IDs (`myChart1`, `myChart2`). Each gets its own canvas+div pair.\n- For bubble and scatter charts: bubble radii extend past their center points, so points near axis boundaries get clipped. Pad the scale range \u2014 set `scales.y.min` and `scales.y.max` ~10% beyond your data range (same for x). Or use `layout: { padding: 20 }` as a blunt fallback.\n- Chart.js auto-skips x-axis labels when they'd overlap. If you have \u226412 categories and need all labels visible (waterfall, monthly series), set `scales.x.ticks: { autoSkip: false, maxRotation: 45 }` \u2014 missing labels make bars unidentifiable.\n\n**Number formatting**: negative values are `-$5M` not `$-5M` \u2014 sign before currency symbol. Use a formatter: `(v) => (v < 0 ? '-' : '') + '$' + Math.abs(v) + 'M'`.\n\n**Legends** \u2014 always disable Chart.js default and build custom HTML. The default uses round dots and no values; custom HTML gives small squares, tight spacing, and percentages:\n\n```js\nplugins: { legend: { display: false } }\n```\n\n```html\n<div style=\"display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 16px; margin-bottom: 8px; font-size: 12px; color: var(--color-text-secondary);\">\n  <span style=\"display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px;\"><span style=\"width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 2px; background: #3266ad;\"></span>Chrome 65%</span>\n  <span style=\"display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px;\"><span style=\"width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 2px; background: #73726c;\"></span>Safari 18%</span>\n</div>\n```\n\nInclude the value/percentage in each label when the data is categorical (pie, donut, single-series bar). Position the legend above the chart (`margin-bottom`) or below (`margin-top`) \u2014 not inside the canvas.\n\n**Dashboard layout** \u2014 wrap summary numbers in metric cards (see UI fragment) above the chart. Chart canvas flows below without a card wrapper. Use `sendPrompt()` for drill-down: `sendPrompt('Break down Q4 by region')`.\n\n## Geographic maps (D3 choropleth)\n\n**Never invent coordinates** \u2014 no hand-drawn SVG paths, no inline GeoJSON. Fetch real topology or don't draw a map.\n\nThree topology sources on jsdelivr. CSP only allows `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `esm.sh`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net`, `unpkg.com` \u2014 do NOT try `raw.githubusercontent.com` or other hosts, the fetch will silently fail. Other package names like `uk-atlas` don't exist (404).\n- US states: `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/us-atlas@3/states-10m.json` \u2192 `d3.geoAlbersUsa()`, object key `.states`\n- World countries: `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/world-atlas@2/countries-110m.json` \u2192 `d3.geoNaturalEarth1()`, object key `.countries`\n- Per-country subdivisions: `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/datamaps@0.5.10/src/js/data/{iso3}.topo.json` (lowercase alpha-3: `deu`, `jpn`, `gbr`...), object key `.{iso3}`\n\n**Before writing the widget, web_fetch the topology URL you'll use.** The first ~1KB shows the real feature `id` and `properties.name` values \u2014 key your data on those, don't guess. Drill all \u00d83mm guide pin holes with hand drill (slow, 500 RPM max)\n2. Drill all \u00d84mm alignment pin holes\n3. Sand bore face (ID=90.7mm): 220 \u2192 400 \u2192 800 grit, CIRCUMFERENTIAL direction\n4. Sand all cam track surfaces: same progression\n5. Wipe with IPA (isopropyl alcohol), let dry 5 minutes\n6. Apply thin West System epoxy to cam faces only \u2014 rotate part slowly, 1 thin coat\n7. Cure 24h at room temp (or 2h at 60\u00b0C in oven)\n8. Sand epoxy: 1000 \u2192 1500 grit wet\n9. Apply PTFE dry lube spray \u2014 2 coats, let dry between coats\n\n### Cylinder:\n1. Inspect all 60 slots \u2014 clear any stringing with dental pick or 0.7mm drill\n2. Verify entry chamfers (0.4mm) are clean and smooth\n3. Sand inner bore (ID=66mm) lightly: 400 grit\n4. Apply PTFE lube to outer surface (OD=90mm) \u2014 this face runs inside cam ring\n\n### Retainer ring (PA12 Nylon):\n1. Verify ID = 92.2mm \u00b10.05mm with calipers\n2. Sand butt track surfaces smooth: 400 grit\n3. Apply PTFE lube to inner contact face\n\n### Cassette base:\n1. Install M5 brass heat inserts \u2014 soldering iron at 200\u00b0C, press in slowly\n2. Press \u00d84mm alignment pins into through-holes (from bottom)\n   - Pins should be snug but not requiring a hammer\n   - If tight: ream holes with \u00d84mm drill\n   - If loose: add thin layer of Loctite 603 retaining compound\n\n---\n\n## STEP 2 \u2014 NEEDLE INSTALLATION\n\n**Do NOT skip this step \u2014 install needles before assembling cassette.**\n\n1. Measure needle blade thickness with calipers (record value)\n2. Verify slot width = blade + 0.10mm clearance\n3. Oil needles lightly with sewing machine oil\n4. Insert each needle into slot from TOP, latch side down\n   - Needle should slide freely with light finger pressure\n   - If tight: lightly sand slot walls (fold 400 grit, run through slot)\n   - If very loose (>0.15mm play): cylinder slot too wide \u2014 reprint\n4. Push needle down until butt engages at slot bottom\n5. Verify latch opens and closes freely on each needle\n6. Needles should be retained by spring friction \u2014 not fall out when inverted\n\n---\n\n## STEP 3 \u2014 CASSETTE BASE ON SHAFT\n\n1. Slide cassette base onto 12mm shaft\n2. Position thrust bearing (51101) directly under base\n3. Install shaft collar below thrust bearing\n4. Tighten collar set screw \u2014 Loctite 243 on threads\n5. Check: base should rotate freely, zero axial play\n6. Install bottom bearing pair (2\u00d7 6001-2RS) in lower housing\n7. Verify shaft vertical: < 0.2mm runout over 200mm height\n\n---\n\n## STEP 4 \u2014 CYLINDER ON BASE\n\n1. Align cylinder key slot with base key slot\n2. Drop cylinder onto base alignment pins (3\u00d7 \u00d84mm)\n   - Pins should enter cylinder blind holes without force\n   - If resistant: check pin/hole alignment, clean holes\n3. Cylinder should sit flush on base top face \u2014 no rocking\n4. Do NOT bolt yet\n\n---\n\n## STEP 5 \u2014 CAM RING INSTALLATION\n\n1. The cam ring does NOT rotate \u2014 it is stationary relative to frame\n2. Position cam ring around cylinder (cylinder is inside cam ring)\n3. Verify radial gap: insert 0.35mm feeler gauge between cylinder OD and cam ID\n   - Should slide freely all around circumference\n   - If gap varies > 0.1mm: check cylinder concentricity on shaft\n4. Drop cam ring alignment pins into base pin holes\n5. Cam ring should sit stable \u2014 zero wobble\n\n---\n\n## STEP 6 \u2014 STITCH CAM INSERTS\n\n1. Insert cam insert #1 into pocket at 90\u00b0 (Feed 1 position)\n2. Guide pins (\u00d83mm) should be pre-pressed into cam body\n3. Insert slides in from bore side \u2014 guide holes align with pins\n4. Adjust radial position: nominal = 3.5mm stitch depth\n5. Lock with 2\u00d7 M3 set screws \u2014 finger tight + 1/8 turn\n6. Repeat for insert #2 at 270\u00b0 (Feed 2 position)\n\n---\n\n## STEP 7 \u2014 SINKER RING\n\n1. Place sinker ring on top of cylinder\n2. Verify sinker nose positions relative to needle hooks\n   - Sinker nose should be just below needle hook centerline at lowest position\n3. Sinker ring is a press/slip fit \u2014 does not bolt separately\n\n---\n\n## STEP 8 \u2014 RETAINER RING\n\n1. Place retainer ring on top of sinker ring\n2. Verify clearance above needle butts: 0.25mm (use feeler gauge)\n3. If too tight: sand retainer ID lightly (400 grit, circumferential)\n\n---\n\n## STEP 9 \u2014 CASSETTE CLAMP BOLTS\n\n1. Install 4\u00d7 M5 \u00d7 25mm through cassette stack into base inserts\n2. Tighten in star pattern (cross-tighten, not sequential)\n3. Torque: 1.5 Nm (finger tight + 1/4 turn with hex key)\n4. Do NOT overtighten \u2014 PETG will creep\n\n---\n\n## STEP 10 \u2014 FUNCTION CHECK\n\n```\nROTATION TEST:\n  Turn shaft by hand \u2014 cylinder should rotate smoothly\n  Needles should rise and fall as they pass cam zones\n  Listen: smooth whisper = good | clicking = cam contact issue\n\nGAP TEST:\n  Insert 0.35mm feeler gauge at multiple points\n  Should pass freely, 0.5mm should NOT pass\n\nNEEDLE TEST:\n  Push individual needles to highest position manually\n  They should stay up (cam hold zone working)\n  Release \u2014 they should descend smoothly\n\nSTITCH DEPTH TEST (without yarn):\n  Mark one needle with paint pen\n  Rotate cylinder slowly \u2014 observe needle travel\n  Maximum lift should be ~12mm\n  Full drop should be ~3.5mm below top\n```\n\n---\n\n## CRITICAL WARNINGS\n\n- **Never force the cam ring** \u2014 if it doesn't slide, find out why. Forcing = damaged bore\n- **Never overtighten clamp bolts** \u2014 1.5 Nm maximum\n- **PTFE lube only** \u2014 NO WD40, NO machine oil on cam surfaces (attracts debris)\n- **Needle slots must be clean** \u2014 one stuck needle can strip all needles at speed\n\n---\n\n*Phase2_Cassette_Assembly.md | V1.0 | April 2026 | CSM V3*\n*Next: Phase3_Drive_Assembly.md*\n",

0.2, TRACK_W + 2)\\nt_out.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, CAM_H / 2.0 - TRACK_W / 2.0))\\nt_in.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, CAM_H / 2.0 - TRACK_W / 2.0 - 1))\\ncam = cam.cut(t_out.cut(t_in))\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# FIX 3: INSERT POCKETS \\u2014 consistent coordinate system\\n# Pocket dimensions use chord (tangential) and radial (depth) correctly\\n# =============================================================================\\n\\ndef make_insert_pocket_corrected(angle_center_deg, cam_body):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    Cut insert pocket at given center angle.\\n    FIX 3: Uses chord dimension for tangential width (not arc length directly)\\n    FIX 4: Cuts BOTH guide pin holes (no break statement)\\n    FIX 5: Set screws positioned near outer face\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    ang_rad = math.radians(angle_center_deg)\\n    \\n    # INSERT POCKET in local coords (centered at angle_center_deg)\\n    # X = tangential (chord direction), Y = radial inward, Z = axial\\n    half_chord = INSERT_CHORD / 2.0\\n    radial_depth = STITCH_Z + BACK_WALL  # full zone + back wall\\n    pocket_z_bot = (CAM_H - INSERT_H) / 2.0\\n\\n    # Full slot (includes back wall material \\u2014 we DON'T cut back wall)\\n    slot = Part.makeBox(SLOT_W, STITCH_Z, INSERT_H)\\n    slot.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(-SLOT_W / 2.0, INSERT_R_IN, pocket_z_bot))\\n    slot.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,1), angle_center_deg)\\n    cam_body = cam_body.cut(slot)\\n    # Back wall (BACK_WALL mm) is NOT cut \\u2014 remains as support shelf\\n\\n    # FIX 4: BOTH guide pin holes (2 \\u00d7 \\u00d83mm) \\u2014 NO break statement\\n    # Pins run tangentially through the cam wall, flanking the insert slot\\n    pin_r_pos = INSERT_R_IN + STITCH_Z / 2.0  # radial midpoint of stitch zone\\n    pin_z_positions = [pocket_z_bot + 4.0, pocket_z_bot + INSERT_H - 4.0]\\n\\n    for pz in pin_z_positions:\\n        # Pin hole: tangential direction through cam wall on each side of slot\\n        for x_side in [-half_chord - PIN_DEPTH/2.0 - 0.5,\\n                        half_chord + PIN_DEPTH/2.0 + 0.5]:\\n            ph = Part.makeCylinder(PIN_HOLE_D / 2.0, PIN_DEPTH)\\n            ph.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,1,0), 90)\\n            ph.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(x_side - PIN_DEPTH, pin_r_pos, pz))\\n            ph.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,1), angle_center_deg)\\n            cam_body = cam_body.cut(ph)\\n\\n    # FIX 5: Set screws near OUTER face (not mid-wall)\\n    # Two screws at \\u00b11/3 of chord length, accessing from outside\\n    for chord_offset in [-half_chord * 0.5, half_chord * 0.5]:\\n        ss = Part.makeCylinder(1.6, CAM_WALL - 2.0)  # M3 tap, stops 2mm from bore\\n        ss.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,1,0), 90)\\n        # Start from outer face, go inward\\n        ss_r_start = CAM_R_OUT - 0.5\\n        ss.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(chord_offset, ss_r_start - (CAM_WALL - 2.0),\\n                                     CAM_H / 2.0))\\n        ss.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,1), angle_center_deg)\\n        cam_body = cam_body.cut(ss)\\n\\n    return cam_body\\n\\nprint(\\\"\\\\nCutting insert pocket #1 at 90\\u00b0 (Feed 1)...\\\")\\ncam = make_insert_pocket_corrected(STITCH1_CEN, cam)\\nprint(\\\"Cutting insert pocket #2 at 270\\u00b0 (Feed 2)...\\\")\\ncam = make_insert_pocket_corrected(STITCH2_CEN, cam)\\nprint(\\\"Both insert pockets complete \\u2705\\\")\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# BOLT HOLES (4\\u00d7 M5 with countersinks)\\n# =============================================================================\\nfor i in range(BOLT_N):\\n    ang = math.radians(i * 90.0 + 45.0)\\n    bx = BOLT_R * math.cos(ang)\\n    by = BOLT_R * math.sin(ang)\\n    bh = Part.makeCylinder(BOLT_D / 2.0, CAM_H + 2)\\n    bh.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(bx, by, -1))\\n    cam = cam.cut(bh)\\n    cs = Part.makeCylinder(4.5, 5.0)\\n    cs.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(bx, by, CAM_H - 5.0))\\n    cam = cam.cut(cs)\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# ALIGNMENT PINS (3\\u00d7 \\u00d84mm, depth 10mm, H7/g6 slip)\\n# =============================================================================\\nfor i in range(APIN_N):\\n    ang = math.radians(i * 120.0 + 30.0)\\n    px = APIN_R * math.cos(ang)\\n    py = APIN_R * math.sin(ang)\\n    ph = Part.makeCylinder(APIN_D / 2.0 + 0.05, APIN_DEPTH)\\n    ph.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(px, py, 0))\\n    cam = cam.cut(ph)\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# KEY SLOT (sliding fit)\\n# =============================================================================\\nks = Part.makeBox(KEY_W + 0.15, KEY_DEPTH + 0.1, KEY_W * 5)\\nks.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(-(KEY_W + 0.15) / 2.0,\\n                              CAM_R_IN - KEY_DEPTH - 0.1,\\n                              CAM_H / 2.0 - KEY_W * 2.5))\\ncam = cam.cut(ks)\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# FINALIZE\\n# =============================================================================\\nobj = doc.addObject(\\\"Part::Feature\\\", \\\"CSM_CamRing_V1_Corrected\\\")\\nobj.Shape = cam\\nobj.ViewObject.ShapeColor = (0.28, 0.28, 0.36)\\ndoc.recompute()\\nFreeCAD.Gui.activeDocument().activeView().viewIsometric()\\nFreeCAD.Gui.SendMsgToActiveView(\\\"ViewFit\\\")\\n\\nvol = cam.Volume\\nprint(f\\\"\\\\n{'='*60}\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"\\u2705 CAM RING V1 CORRECTED \\u2014 COMPLETE\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"{'='*60}\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   OD={CAM_OD}  ID={CAM_ID}  H={CAM_H}\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   Volume: {vol:.0f}mm\\u00b3  PETG: {vol*1.27/1000:.1f}g  Al: {vol*2.70/1000:.1f}g\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"\\\\n6 FIXES CONFIRMED:\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   \\u2705 Fix 1: Functional R(theta) cam profile (72-point polygon)\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   \\u2705 Fix 2: Angular sector geometry (no full-ring cuts)\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   \\u2705 Fix 3: Chord dimensions for insert pocket\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   \\u2705 Fix 4: Both guide pin holes cut (no break)\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"   \\u2705 Fix 5: Set screws at outer face (CAM_R_OUT - C:\\3D-Project\\01_MECHANICAL\\02_CASSETTE_HEAD\\cam_ring\\freecad_macros\\\n#\n# FIXES APPLIED IN V2 (all 4 confirmed by engineering review):\n#\n#   FIX 1 \u2014 Lower zone formula corrected\n#     Old: R_BASE + (LIFT-STITCH_DROP)*(1-x)**2  \u2190 too steep at start\n#     New: R_BASE + (LIFT-STITCH_DROP)*(1+cos(pi*x))/2  \u2190 symmetric cosine\n#     Effect: smooth deceleration, eliminates butt impact/clicking\n#\n#   FIX 2 \u2014 LIFT increased 10.0 \u2192 11.0mm\n#     12G latch needles typically need 10.5\u201312mm for complete loop clearing\n#     11.0mm: safe compromise, still constant\n#   Stitch: 80\u00b0\u2013140\u00b0 linear (controlled by insert \u00b11.5mm)\n#   Lower:  140\u00b0\u2013170\u00b0 cosine ease-out (FIXED symmetric)\n#   Idle:   170\u00b0\u2013180\u00b0 neutral\n#   2-feed: profile repeats at 180\u00b0 \u2014 inserts at 90\u00b0 and 270\u00b0\n#\n# FULL PROFILE (key angles):\n#   \u03b8=  0\u00b0  R=45.350mm  depth=0.000mm  [RAISE start]\n#   \u03b8= 25\u00b0  R=50.863mm  depth=5.513mm  [mid-raise]\n#   \u03b8= 50\u00b0  R=56.350mm  depth=11.000mm [HOLD peak]\n#   \u03b8= 80\u00b0  R=56.350mm  depth=11.000mm [STITCH start]\n#   \u03b8=110\u00b0  R=55.283mm  depth=9.933mm  [stitch mid]\n#   \u03b8=140\u00b0  R=53.150mm  depth=7.800mm  [LOWER start]\n#   \u03b8=155\u00b0  R=49.250mm  depth=3.900mm  [lower mid]\n#   \u03b8=170\u00b0  R=45.350mm  depth=0.000mm  [IDLE neutral]\n# =============================================================================\n\nimport FreeCAD, Part, math\n\ndoc = FreeCAD.newDocument(\"CSM_CamRing_Conservative_V2\")\n\n# =============================================================================\n# LOCKED PARAMETERS \u2014 ALL CONFIRMED\n# =============================================================================\n\nCAM_ID      = 90.7       # mm \u2014 LOCKED (0.35mm radial gap to cylinder)\nCAM_OD      = 140.0      # mm \u2014 LOCKED\nCAM_H       = 25.0       # mm \u2014 LOCKED\nCYL_OD      = 90.0       # mm \u2014 LOCKED\nCAM_WALL    = (CAM_OD - CAM_ID) / 2.0   # 24.65mm\n\nR_BASE      = CAM_ID / 2.0    # 45.35mm \u2014 neutral radius (no cam contact)\nCAM_R_OUT   = CAM_OD / 2.0   # 70.0mm\n\n# Conservative profile \u2014 V2 values (all 4 fixes applied)\nLIFT        = 11.0   # mm \u2014 FIX 2: was 10.0mm (too low for loop clearing)\nSTITCH_DROP = 3.2    # mm \u2014 nominal stitch cam depth (insert adjusts \u00b11.5mm)\nPOINTS      = 288    # FIX 4: was 144 (chord error now ~0\u00b5m)\n\n# Cam zone radial widths\nRAISE_Z     = 6.0    # mm radial\nGUARD_Z     = 3.0\nSTITCH_Z    = 8.0\nLOWER_Z     = 5.0\n\n# Track groove \u2014 FIX 3\nTRACK_W     = 2.1    # mm \u2014 butt 2.0mm + 0.10mm total (measure real needle!)\nTRACK_D     = 3.3    # mm \u2014 FIX 3: was 2.5mm (lateral stability at speed)\n\n# Insert geometry \u2014 corrected coordinate system (chord, not arc)\nR_STITCH_CEN = R_BASE + RAISE_Z + GUARD_Z + STITCH_Z / 2.0  # 58.35mm\nINSERT_ARC   = 22.0   # mm arc length\narc_ang_rad  = INSERT_ARC / R_STITCH_CEN\nINSERT_CHORD = 2 * R_STITCH_CEN * math.sin(arc_ang_rad / 2)  # ~21.87mm\nINSERT_W     = 7.65   # mm \u2014 insert body width\nSLOT_W       = 8.0    # mm \u2014 pocket width (0.175mm clearance/side)\nINSERT_H     = 20.0   # mm \u2014 axial height\nINSERT_R_IN  = R_BASE + RAISE_Z + GUARD_Z   # 54.35mm \u2014 inner face of stitch zone\nBACK_WALL    = 1.0    # mm \u2014 rear support wall (NOT cut)\nSTITCH1_ANG  = 90.0   # \u00b0 \u2014 insert #1 center (Feed 1)\nSTITCH2_ANG  = 270.0  # \u00b0 \u2014 insert #2 center (Feed 2)\n\n# Guide pins \u2014 \u00d83mm slip fit\nPIN_D        = 3.0\nPIN_HOLE_D   = 3.1    # H7/g6\nPIN_DEPTH    = 10.0\n\n# Cassette interface \u2014 all locked\nSHAFT_CLEAR  = 12.0 / 2.0 + 0.5   # 6.5mm radius (13mm hole)\nBOLT_PCD     = 130.0\nBOLT_N       = 4\nBOLT_D       = 5.5\nAPIN_PCD     = 120.0\nAPIN_N       = 3\nAPIN_D       = 4.0\nAPIN_DEPTH   = 10.0\nKEY_W        = 3.0\nKEY_DEPTH    = 1.5\n\nBOLT_R  = BOLT_PCD / 2.0\nAPIN_R  = APIN_PCD / 2.0\n\n# =============================================================================\n# R(theta) \u2014 CONSERVATIVE CAM PROFILE  V2\n# All 4 fixes applied. Continuous, smooth, no step changes.\n# =============================================================================\ndef cam_radius(theta_deg):\n    \"\"\"\n    Conservative cam profile for 12G latch needles at 60\u2013120 RPM on PETG cam.\n    Returns inner radius of cam at angle theta_deg.\n    R > R_BASE: cam extends inward, pushes needle butt up, lifts needle.\n    2-feed: profile repeats every 180\u00b0.\n    \"\"\"\n    t = theta_deg % 180.0\n\n    if t < 50.0:\n        # RAISE \u2014 cosine ease-in (smooth acceleration, minimal butt shock)\n        x = t / 50.0\n        return R_BASE + LIFT * (1.0 - math.cos(math.pi * x)) / 2.0\n\n    elif t < 80.0:\n        # HOLD \u2014 constant max (needle fully raised, yarn enters hook)\n        return R_BASE + LIFT\n\n    elif t < 140.0:\n        # STITCH \u2014 linear drop (insert fine-tunes final stitch depth)\n        x = (t - 80.0) / 60.0\n        return R_BASE + LIFT - STITCH_DROP * x\n\n    elif t < 170.0:\n        # LOWER \u2014 FIX 1: symmetric cosine ease-out (was quadratic \u2014 too steep)\n        # Symmetric cosine matches raise profile, eliminates butt impact\n        x = (t - 140.0) / 30.0\n        return R_BASE + (LIFT - STITCH_DROP) * (1.0 + math.cos(math.pi * x)) / 2.0\n\n    else:\n        # IDLE / TRANSITION \u2014 neutral (no cam contact)\n        return R_BASE\n\n# =============================================================================\n# BUILD 288-POINT CAM PROFILE POLYGON\n# =============================================================================\nprint(\"=\" * 55)\nprint(\"CSM V3 CAM RING \u2014 CONSERVATIVE V2\")\nprint(\"=\" * 55)\nprint(f\"  Lift={LIFT}mm  Drop={STITCH_DROP}mm  Points={POINTS}\")\nprint(f\"  CAM_ID={CAM_ID}mm  CAM_OD={CAM_OD}mm  H={CAM_H}mm\")\nprint(f\"  Track: W={TRACK_W}mm D={TRACK_D}mm\")\nprint()\nprint(\"Building profile polygon...\")\n\npts = []\nfor i in range(POINTS):\n    ang_rad = 2.0 * math.pi * i / POINTS\n    ang_deg = math.degrees(ang_rad)\n    r = cam_radius(ang_deg)\n    pts.append(FreeCAD.Vector(\n        r * math.cos(ang_rad),\n        r * math.sin(ang_rad),\n        0.0\n    ))\npts.append(pts[0])  # close\n\nwire = Part.makePolygon(pts)\nface = Part.Face(wire)\nprofile_solid = face.extrude(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, CAM_H))\nprint(f\"  Profile solid: {POINTS} points, 1.25\u00b0/step\")\n\n# =============================================================================\n# BUILD OUTER RING AND SUBTRACT PROFILE\n# =============================================================================\nouter = Part.makeCylinder(CAM_R_OUT, CAM_H)\ncam   = outer.cut(profile_solid)\nprint(\"  Outer ring - profile = cam body \u2705\")\n\n# Shaft clearance (13mm hole \u2014 not structural load path)\nshft = Part.makeCylinder(SHAFT_CLEAR, CAM_H + 2)\nshft.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, -1))\ncam = cam.cut(shft)\n\n# =============================================================================\n# REGISTRATION GROOVE \u2014 lateral butt guidance (not load bearing)\n# FIX 3: TRACK_D=3.3mm prevents butt climbing at speed\n# =============================================================================\nt_out = Part.makeCylinder(R_BASE + TRACK_D, TRACK_W)\nt_in  = Part.makeCylinder(R_BASE - 0.1, TRACK_W + 2)\nt_out.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, CAM_H / 2.0 - TRACK_W / 2.0))\nt_in.translate( FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, CAM_H / 2.0 - TRACK_W / 2.0 - 1))\ncam = cam.cut(t_out.cut(t_in))\nprint(f\"  Registration groove: W={TRACK_W}mm D={TRACK_D}mm \u2705\")\n\n# =============================================================================\n# INSERT POCKETS \u2014 Feed 1 at 90\u00b0, Feed 2 at 270\u00b0\n# =============================================================================\ndef make_insert_pocket(center_ang_deg, cam_body):\n    half_chord = INSERT_CHORD / 2.0\n    pz_bot = (CAM_H - INSERT_H) / 2.0  # 2.5mm from bottom\n\n    # Main slot \u2014 stitch zone width, back wall remains solid\n    slot = Part.makeBox(SLOT_W, STITCH_Z, INSERT_H)\n    slot.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(-SLOT_W / 2.0, INSERT_R_IN, pz_bot))\n    slot.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,1), center_ang_deg)\n    cam_body = cam_body.cut(slot)\n\n    # Guide pin holes: 2 per insert, both Z positions (no break \u2014 Fix 4 retained)\n    pin_r = INSERT_R_IN + STITCH_Z / 2.0\n    for pz in [pz_bot + 4.0, pz_bot + INSERT_H - 4.0]:\n        ph = Part.makeCylinder(PIN_HOLE_D / 2.0, PIN_DEPTH + 2)\n        ph.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,1,0), 90)\n        ph.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(\n            -half_chord - PIN_DEPTH - 1,\n            pin_r, pz\n        ))\n        ph.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,1), center_ang_deg)\n        cam_body = cam_body.cut(ph)\n\n    # Set screws: 2\u00d7 M3 from outer face (Fix 5 retained)\n    for chord_off in [-half_chord * 0.5, half_chord * 0.5]:\n        ss = Part.makeCylinder(1.6, CAM_WALL - 2.0)\n        ss.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,1,0), 90)\n        ss.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(\n            chord_off,\n            CAM_R_OUT - (CAM_WALL - 2.0) - 0.5,\n            CAM_H / 2.0\n        ))\n        ss.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,1), center_ang_deg)\n        cam_body = cam_body.cut(ss)\n\n    return cam_body\n\ncam = make_insert_pocket(STITCH1_ANG, cam)\nprint(\"  Insert pocket #1 at 90\u00b0 \u2705\")\ncam = make_insert_pocket(STITCH2_ANG, cam)\nprint(\"  Insert pocket #2 at 270\u00b0 \u2705\")\n\n# =============================================================================\n# BOLT HOLES \u2014 4\u00d7 M5 with countersinks\n# =============================================================================\nfor i in range(BOLT_N):\n    ang = math.radians(i * 90.0 + 45.0)\n    bx, by = BOLT_R * math.cos(ang), BOLT_R * math.sin(ang)\n    bh = Part.makeCylinder(BOLT_D / 2.0, CAM_H + 2)\n    bh.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(bx, by, -1))\n    cam = cam.cut(bh)\n    cs = Part.makeCylinder(4.5, 5.0)\n    cs.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(bx, by, CAM_H - 5.0))\n    cam = cam.cut(cs)\n\n# =============================================================================\n# ALIGNMENT PINS \u2014 3\u00d7 \u00d84mm, 10mm depth, H7/g6 slip\n# =============================================================================\nfor i in range(APIN_N):\n    ang = math.radians(i * 120.0 + 30.0)\n    px, py = APIN_R * math.cos(ang), APIN_R * math.sin(ang)\n    ph = Part.makeCylinder(APIN_D / 2.0 + 0.05, APIN_DEPTH)\n    ph.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(px, py, 0))\n    cam = cam.cut(ph)\n\n# =============================================================================\n# KEY SLOT \u2014 sliding fit\n# =============================================================================\nks = Part.makeBox(KEY_W + 0.15, KEY_DEPTH + 0.1, KEY_W * 5)\nks.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(\n    -(KEY_W + 0.15) / 2.0,\n    R_BASE - KEY_DEPTH - 0.1,\n    CAM_H / 2.0 - KEY_W * 2.5\n))\ncam = cam.cut(ks)\n\n# =============================================================================\n# SOLENOID RESERVE GROOVE (outer face identification mark)\n# =============================================================================\nsg = Part.makeCylinder(CAM_R_OUT - 0.5, 1.5)\nsi = Part.makeCylinder(CAM_R_OUT - 3.0, 2.5)\nsg.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, 1.0))\nsi.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, 0.5))\ncam = cam.cut(sg.cut(si))\n\n# =============================================================================\n# FINALIZE\n# =============================================================================\nobj = doc.addObject(\"Part::Feature\", \"CSM_CamRing_Conservative_V2\")\nobj.Shape = cam\nobj.ViewObject.ShapeColor = (0.15, 0.35, 0.60)\ndoc.recompute()\nFreeCAD.Gui.activeDocument().activeView().viewIsometric()\nFreeCAD.Gui.SendMsgToActiveView(\"ViewFit\")\n\nvol = cam.Volume\nprint()\nprint(\"=\" * 55)\nprint(\"\u2705 CAM RING CONSERVATIVE V2 \u2014 COMPLETE\")\nprint(\"=\" * 55)\nprint(f\"  Volume: {vol:.0f}mm\u00b3\")\nprint(f\"  Weight PETG: {vol*1.27/1000:.1f}g\")\nprint(f\"  Weight Al:   {vol*2.70/1000:.1f}g\")\nprint()\nprint(\"V2 FIXES CONFIRMED:\")\nprint(\"  \u2705 Fix 1: Lower zone \u2192 symmetric cosine (no butt shock)\")\nprint(\"  \u2705 Fix 2: LIFT = 11.0mm (complete loop clearing)\")\nprint(\"  \u2705 Fix 3: TRACK_D = 3.3mm (lateral stability at speed)\")\nprint(\"  \u2705 Fix 4: POINTS = 288 (chord error ~0\u00b5m)\")\nprint()\nprint(\"SAVE TO:\")\nprint(\"  C:\\\\3D-Project\\\\01_MECHANICAL\\\\02_CASSETTE_HEAD\\\\\")\nprint(\"  cam_ring\\\\freecad_macros\\\\\")\nprint()\nprint(\"POST-PROCESS (mandatory):\")\nprint(\"  1. Sand: 220 \u2192 400 \u2192 800 grit CIRCUMFERENTIAL\")\nprint(\"  5. West System epoxy thin coat \u2192 cure 24h\")\nprint(\"  6. Wet sand: 1000 \u2192 1500 grit\")\nprint(\"  7. PTFE dry lube (2 coats, dry between)\")\nprint(\"  8. TEST: one-finger rotation = ready\")\nprint()\nprint(\"TUNING SEQUENCE:\")\nprint(\"  Start:  30 RPM break-in (50 revolutions)\")\nprint(\"  Then:   60 RPM (normal operation)\")\nprint(\"  Target: 90\u2013120 RPM max (PETG cam)\")\nprint(\"  Stitch: start at 3.2mm, adjust insert \u00b11.5mm\")\nprint()\nprint(\"UPGRADE PATH:\")\nprint(\"  Print aggressive profile (V_Aggressive.FCMacro)\")\nprint(\"  \u2192 when aluminum cam is ready for CNC\")\nprint(\"  \u2192 raise 0\u00b0\u201330\u00b0, LIFT=12mm, RPM 120+\")\n",

140.0) / 30.0\\n        return R_BASE + (LIFT - STITCH_DROP) * (1.0 + math.cos(math.pi * x)) / 2.0\\n\\n    else:\\n        # IDLE / TRANSITION \\u2014 neutral (no cam contact)\\n        return R_BASE\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# BUILD 288-POINT CAM PROFILE POLYGON\\n# =============================================================================\\nprint(\\\"=\\\" * 55)\\nprint(\\\"CSM V3 CAM RING \\u2014 CONSERVATIVE V2\\\")\\nprint(\\\"=\\\" * 55)\\nprint(f\\\"  Lift={LIFT}mm  Drop={STITCH_DROP}mm  Points={POINTS}\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  CAM_ID={CAM_ID}mm  CAM_OD={CAM_OD}mm  H={CAM_H}mm\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  Track: W={TRACK_W}mm D={TRACK_D}mm\\\")\\nprint()\\nprint(\\\"Building profile polygon...\\\")\\n\\npts = []\\nfor i in range(POINTS):\\n    ang_rad = 2.0 * math.pi * i / POINTS\\n    ang_deg = math.degrees(ang_rad)\\n    r = cam_radius(ang_deg)\\n    pts.append(FreeCAD.Vector(\\n        r * math.cos(ang_rad),\\n        r * math.sin(ang_rad),\\n        0.0\\n    ))\\npts.append(pts[0])  # close\\n\\nwire = Part.makePolygon(pts)\\nface = Part.Face(wire)\\nprofile_solid = face.extrude(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, CAM_H))\\nprint(f\\\"  Profile solid: {POINTS} points, 1.25\\u00b0/step\\\")\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# BUILD OUTER RING AND SUBTRACT PROFILE\\n# =============================================================================\\nouter = Part.makeCylinder(CAM_R_OUT, CAM_H)\\ncam   = outer.cut(profile_solid)\\nprint(\\\"  Outer ring - profile = cam body \\u2705\\\")\\n\\n# Shaft clearance (13mm hole \\u2014 not structural load path)\\nshft = Part.makeCylinder(SHAFT_CLEAR, CAM_H + 2)\\nshft.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, -1))\\ncam = cam.cut(shft)\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# REGISTRATION GROOVE \\u2014 lateral butt guidance (not load bearing)\\n# FIX 3: TRACK_D=3.3mm prevents butt climbing at speed\\n# =============================================================================\\nt_out = Part.makeCylinder(R_BASE + TRACK_D, TRACK_W)\\nt_in  = Part.makeCylinder(R_BASE - INSERT_H) / 2.0  # 2.5mm from bottom\\n\\n    # Main slot \\u2014 stitch zone width, back wall remains solid\\n    slot = Part.makeBox(SLOT_W, STITCH_Z, INSERT_H)\\n    slot.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(-SLOT_W / 2.0, INSERT_R_IN, pz_bot))\\n    slot.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,1), center_ang_deg)\\n    cam_body = cam_body.cut(slot)\\n\\n    # Guide pin holes: 2 per insert, both Z positions (no break \\u2014 Fix 4 retained)\\n    pin_r = INSERT_R_IN + STITCH_Z / 2.0\\n    for pz in [pz_bot + 4.0, pz_bot + INSERT_H - PIN_DEPTH - 1,\\n            pin_r, pz\\n        ))\\n        ph.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,1), center_ang_deg)\\n        cam_body = cam_body.cut(ph)\\n\\n    # Set screws: 2\\u00d7 M3 from outer face (Fix 5 retained)\\n    for chord_off in [-half_chord * 0.5, half_chord * 0.5]:\\n        ss = Part.makeCylinder(1.6, CAM_WALL - 2.0)\\n        ss.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,1,0), 90)\\n        ss.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(\\n            chord_off,\\n            CAM_R_OUT - (CAM_WALL - 2.0) - 0.5,\\n            CAM_H / 2.0\\n        ))\\n        ss.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,1), center_ang_deg)\\n        cam_body = cam_body.cut(ss)\\n\\n    return cam_body\\n\\ncam = make_insert_pocket(STITCH1_ANG, cam)\\nprint(\\\"  Insert pocket #1 at 90\\u00b0 \\u2705\\\")\\ncam = make_insert_pocket(STITCH2_ANG, cam)\\nprint(\\\"  Insert pocket #2 at 270\\u00b0 \\u2705\\\")\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# BOLT HOLES \\u2014 4\\u00d7 M5 with countersinks\\n# =============================================================================\\nfor i in range(BOLT_N):\\n    ang = math.radians(i * 90.0 + 45.0)\\n    bx, by = BOLT_R * math.cos(ang), BOLT_R * math.sin(ang)\\n    bh = Part.makeCylinder(BOLT_D / 2.0, CAM_H + 2)\\n    bh.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(bx, by, -1))\\n    cam = cam.cut(bh)\\n    cs = Part.makeCylinder(4.5, 5.0)\\n    cs.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(bx, by, CAM_H - 0.5 (was -2.0 \\u2014 limited clamping)\\n    ss_len = CAM_WALL - 0.5\\n    for chord_off in [-half * 0.5, half * 0.5]:\\n        ss = Part.makeCylinder(1.6, ss_len)\\n        ss.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,1,0), 90)\\n        ss.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(\\n            chord_off,\\n            CAM_R_OUT - ss_len,\\n            CAM_H / 2.0\\n        ))\\n        ss.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,1), center_ang_deg)\\n        body = body.cut(ss)\\n\\n    return body\\n\\ncam = insert_pocket(STITCH1_ANG, cam)\\nprint(\\\"  Insert pocket #1 @ 90\\u00b0 \\u2705\\\")\\ncam = insert_pocket(STITCH2_ANG, cam)\\nprint(\\\"  Insert pocket #2 @ 270\\u00b0 \\u2705\\\")\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# BOLT HOLES \\u2014 4\\u00d7 M5\\n# =============================================================================\\nfor i in range(4):\\n    ang = math.radians(i * 90.0 + 45.0)\\n    bx, by = BOLT_R * math.cos(ang), BOLT_R * math.sin(ang)\\n    bh = Part.makeCylinder(5.5 / 2.0, CAM_H + 2)\\n    bh.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(bx, by, -1))\\n    cam = cam.cut(bh)\\n    cs = Part.makeCylinder(4.5, 5.0)\\n    cs.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(bx, by, CAM_H - 5.0))\\n    cam = cam.cut(cs)\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# ALIGNMENT PINS \\u2014 3\\u00d7 \\u00d84mm\\n# =============================================================================\\nfor i in range(APIN_N):\\n    ang = math.radians(i * 120.0 + 30.0)\\n    px, py = APIN_R * math.cos(ang), APIN_R * math.sin(ang)\\n    ph = Part.makeCylinder(APIN_D / 2.0 + 0.05, APIN_DEPTH)\\n    ph.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(px, py, 0))\\n    cam = cam.cut(ph)\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# KEY SLOT \\u2014 sliding fit\\n# =============================================================================\\nks = Part.makeBox(KEY_W + 0.15, KEY_DEPTH + 0.1, KEY_W * 5)\\nks.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(\\n    -(KEY_W + 0.15) / 2.0,\\n    R_BASE - KEY_DEPTH - 0.1,\\n    CAM_H / 2.0 - KEY_W * 2.5\\n))\\ncam = cam.cut(ks)\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# FINALIZE\\n# =============================================================================\\nobj = doc.addObject(\\\"Part::Feature\\\", \\\"CSM_CamRing_V3_Final\\\")\\nobj.Shape = cam\\nobj.ViewObject.ShapeColor = (0.15, 0.32, 0.58)\\ndoc.recompute()\\nFreeCAD.Gui.activeDocument().activeView().viewIsometric()\\nFreeCAD.Gui.SendMsgToActiveView(\\\"ViewFit\\\")\\n\\nvol = cam.Volume\\nprint(f\\\"\\\\n{'='*55}\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"\\u2705 CAM RING V3 FINAL \\u2014 COMPLETE\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"{'='*55}\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  Volume: {vol:.0f}mm\\u00b3\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  PETG:  {vol*1.27/1000:.1f}g | Al: {vol*2.70/1000:.1f}g\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"\\\\n  Fixes applied: 9 total (4 from V2 + 5 new in V3)\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  Boundary continuity: all zones \\u2705\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  Multi-needle overlap: 10 in stitch, 6.7 in yarn window \\u2705\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"\\\\n  Save to:\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  C:\\\\\\\\3D-Project\\\\\\\\01_MECHANICAL\\\\\\\\02_CASSETTE_HEAD\\\\\\\\cam_ring\\\\\\\\freecad_macros\\\\\\\\\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"\\\\n  Post-process: sand \\u2192 IPA \\u2192 epoxy \\u2192 cure \\u2192 polish \\u2192 PTFE\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  First run: 30 RPM break-in \\u2192 60 RPM \\u2192 tune inserts\\\")\\n\", \"filename\": \"/mnt/user-data/outputs/CSM_V3_CamRing_Conservative_V3_Final.FCMacro\"}"

You measure the center-to-center distance between the two pulleys\n\nThen the correct belt length = `2 \u00d7 center_distance + belt_around_pulleys`.\n\nOrder **2 different belt lengths** once you measure:\n- One belt at your calculated length\n- One belt one size up/down as backup\n\n## Updated drive system BOM entries\n\nReplace these three lines:\n\n```\n\u274c GT2 pulley 20T    Bore 10mm   1   $6\n\u274c GT2 pulley 60T    Bore 12mm   1   $10  \n\u274c GT2 belt          6mm \u00d7 280-320mm   2   $5 ea\n```\n\nWith:\n\n```\n\u2705 GT2 pulley 20T    Bore 14mm with keyway, 6mm belt width   1   ~$10\n\u2705 GT2 pulley 60T    Bore 12mm, 6mm belt width               1   ~$12\n\u23f3 GT2 closed-loop belt  6mm wide \u2014 DO NOT ORDER YET, measure after motor mount installed\n```\n\n## Summary\n\n**Original BOM had error:** 10mm bore pulley \u2014 does not match any real NEMA 23 gearbox\n**Corrected:** 14mm bore with keyway for small pulley, 12mm for large pulley unchanged\n**Belt:** Do not order yet, wait until physical layout is measured\n\nReady for me to help find the specific pulley products on Amazon, or do you want to search yourself with the terms above?",

First, an important reality check on the small pulley:\n\n## \u26a0\ufe0f Important discovery \u2014 20T GT2 with 14mm bore is VERY rare\n\n**Why:** A GT2 20T pulley has an outer diameter of only ~12mm. You cannot physically drill a 14mm bore through a 12mm pulley \u2014 the math doesn't work. GT2 pulleys were designed for 3D printer small motors with small shafts (5\u20138mm). 14mm bore requires a larger tooth count.\n\nMost 14mm bore pulleys use either **HTD 5M** (larger pitch) or require a larger tooth count like 40T+.\n\n## Solution: Change belt system from GT2 to HTD 5M (better for your application anyway)\n\n**HTD 5M** is designed for higher torque transmission and larger shafts. The output pin provides an analog output representing if a magnetic field is present, how strong a present field is, and if it is a north or south polar field. If no magnetic field is present the SS49E will output a voltage around half of the source voltage. Just provide power to the GND and VCC pins of the SS49E and connect its output pin to an analog input on your microcontroller or SBC, which you can then measure the analog voltage of to calculate the sensor's measured data. So why use a Hall-effect sensor? Hall-effect sensors are immune to most environmental disturbances that may affect optical or mechanical devices, such as vibration, moisture, dirt or oil films, ambient lighting, etc. Also, they are a simple way to measure the presence of a magnet and even electrical current running through a conductor. os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True)\n\ndoc = FreeCAD.newDocument(\"CSM_BearingHousings_V2\")\n\n# =============================================================================\n# BEARING SPECIFICATIONS\n# =============================================================================\nBEARING_OD      = 28.0    # 6001-2RS outer\nBEARING_ID      = 12.0    # 6001-2RS inner (matches shaft)\nBEARING_W       = 8.0     # 6001-2RS width\n\nTHRUST_OD       = 26.0    # 51101 outer\nTHRUST_ID       = 12.0    # 51101 inner\nTHRUST_H        = 9.0     # 51101 height\nTHRUST_WASHER_OD = 26.0   # Steel washer matches thrust OD\nTHRUST_WASHER_T  = 1.5    # Washer thickness\n\nSHAFT_D         = 12.0    # main shaft diameter\nSHAFT_CLEAR     = 12.5    # REDUCED from 13.0 -- tighter fit (Fix #9)\n\n# =============================================================================\n# FIT TOLERANCES (REVISED V2)\n# =============================================================================\n# Fix #1: SLIP FIT instead of press fit, use Loctite 603 for locking\nSLIP_FIT        = 0.05    # pocket is 0.05mm LARGER than bearing OD\nPOCKET_SLIP     = 0.30    # thrust bearing pocket clearance (unchanged)\n\n# Fix #2: Retaining lip prevents axial migration\nRETAINING_LIP_H = 1.5     # lip height at pocket bottom\nRETAINING_LIP_ID = SHAFT_CLEAR  # inner diameter matches shaft bore\nRETAINING_LIP_OD = BEARING_OD - 2.0  # supports outer race\n\n# =============================================================================\n# TOP BLOCK PARAMETERS (unchanged size - only 1 bearing, small loads)\n# =============================================================================\nTOP_W           = 60.0\nTOP_D           = 60.0\nTOP_H           = 20.0\n# Fix #1: Slip fit = bearing OD + 0.05mm\nTOP_BEARING_POCKET_D = BEARING_OD + SLIP_FIT   # 28.05mm\nTOP_BEARING_POCKET_H = BEARING_W + 0.5         # 8.5mm deep\nTOP_BOLT_PCD    = 48.0\nTOP_BOLT_D      = 5.5     # M5 clearance\nTOP_BOLT_CS_D_TOP = 10.0  # countersink top diameter (head flush)\nTOP_BOLT_CS_H   = 2.8     # M5 head depth (DIN 7991 standard)\n\n# =============================================================================\n# BOTTOM BLOCK PARAMETERS (Fix #6: ENLARGED to 80x80x35)\n# =============================================================================\nBOT_W           = 80.0    # was 70 -- more material around pocket\nBOT_D           = 80.0    # was 70\nBOT_H           = 35.0    # was 30 -- deeper stack + more insert thread\n\n# Fix #4: ONE radial bearing per block (not 2 stacked)\n# Stack bottom-to-top:\n#   3mm floor\n#   1.5mm steel washer (slip fit pocket)\n#   9mm thrust bearing 51101 (slip fit pocket)\n#   1.5mm steel washer (slip fit pocket)\n#   8mm radial bearing 6001-2RS (slip fit + Loctite)\n#   remainder = solid top material\n#\n# Total used: 3 + 1.5 + 9 + 1.5 + 8 = 23mm\n# Solid top: 35 - 23 = 12mm (good thread engagement for heat-set inserts)\n\nBOT_FLOOR_H     = 3.0      # solid floor under washer\nBOT_WASHER_POCKET_D = THRUST_WASHER_OD + # 28.05mm\nBOT_RADIAL_POCKET_H = BEARING_W + 0.5                 # 8.5mm\n\nBOT_BOLT_PCD    = 64.0    # larger PCD for larger block\nBOT_BOLT_D      = 5.5\nBOT_BOLT_CS_D_TOP = 10.0\nBOT_BOLT_CS_H   = 2.8\n\n# Both blocks -- common features\nCHAMFER_SIZE    = 1.0     # Fix #8: now actually applied\n\n# =============================================================================\n# HELPER FUNCTIONS\n# =============================================================================\ndef make_countersink_cone(r_bottom, r_top, height):\n    \"\"\"Fix #5: Proper 90 degree cone for countersink (not a cylinder)\"\"\"\n    # M5 flathead DIN 7991: 90 degree head angle = 45 degree wall from vertical\n    # r_bottom = shank clearance radius (5.5/2 = 2.75mm)\n    # r_top    = head diameter (10/2 = 5mm)\n    # height   = (r_top - r_bottom) for 90 degree cone\n    return Part.makeCone(r_bottom, r_top, height)\n\ndef apply_outer_chamfer(shape, size):\n    \"\"\"Fix #8: Apply chamfer to outer vertical edges for print quality\"\"\"\n    try:\n        edges_to_chamfer = []\n        for i, edge in enumerate(shape.Edges):\n            # Only chamfer vertical edges (corners of the box)\n            v1, v2 = edge.Vertexes[0].Point, edge.Vertexes[1].Point\n            if abs(v1.z - v2.z) > 1.0:  # vertical edge\n                edges_to_chamfer.append(edge)\n        if edges_to_chamfer:\n            return shape.makeChamfer(size, edges_to_chamfer)\n        return shape\n    except Exception as e:\n        print(f\"  Chamfer skipped: {e}\")\n        return shape\n\n# =============================================================================\n# BUILD TOP BLOCK\n# =============================================================================\nprint(\"=\" * 65)\nprint(\"CSM V3 -- BEARING HOUSING BLOCKS V2 (ALL 7 FIXES APPLIED)\")\nprint(\"=\" * 65)\nprint(f\"\\n[1/2] Building TOP block...\")\n\ntop = Part.makeBox(TOP_W, TOP_D, TOP_H)\ntop.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(-TOP_W / 2.0, -TOP_D / 2.0, 0))\n\n# Bearing pocket from TOP face (open top -- bearing inserts from above)\n# Pocket depth = bearing width + 0.5mm clearance\npocket = Part.makeCylinder(TOP_BEARING_POCKET_D / 2.0, TOP_BEARING_POCKET_H)\npocket.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, TOP_H - TOP_BEARING_POCKET_H))\ntop = top.cut(pocket)\n\n# Fix #2: Retaining lip at pocket bottom\n# The lip is formed by NOT cutting a full cylinder -- instead the shaft bore\n# below the pocket is smaller than the bearing OD, creating a shoulder\n# that the bearing rests on. Already achieved by the difference between\n# pocket diameter (28.05) and shaft bore (12.5) -- that ring IS the lip.\n# Lip thickness = (28.05 - 12.5) / 2 = 7.77mm radial -- plenty of support\n\n# Shaft through-hole (Fix #9: reduced to 12.5mm)\nthrough = Part.makeCylinder(SHAFT_CLEAR / 2.0, TOP_H + 2)\nthrough.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, -1))\ntop = top.cut(through)\n\n# Fix #5: 4x M5 bolt holes with PROPER 90 degree countersinks on bottom mount face\nfor i in range(4):\n    ang = math.radians(i * 90.0 + 45.0)\n    bx = (TOP_BOLT_PCD / 2.0) * math.cos(ang)\n    by = (TOP_BOLT_PCD / 2.0) * math.sin(ang)\n    # Shank clearance hole through full height\n    bh = Part.makeCylinder(TOP_BOLT_D / 2.0, TOP_H + 2)\n    bh.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(bx, by, -1))\n    top = top.cut(bh)\n    # Proper conical countersink on BOTTOM mount face\n    # Cone: bottom radius = head diameter, top radius = shank radius\n    cs = make_countersink_cone(TOP_BOLT_CS_D_TOP / 2.0, TOP_BOLT_D / 2.0, TOP_BOLT_CS_H)\n    cs.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(bx, by, 0))\n    top = top.cut(cs)\n\n# Fix #8: Apply outer chamfer for print quality\ntop = apply_outer_chamfer(top, CHAMFER_SIZE)\n\n# Position for visualization (left side)\ntop.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(-60, 0, 0))\n\nobj_top = doc.addObject(\"Part::Feature\", \"BearingHousing_TOP_V2\")\nobj_top.Shape = top\nobj_top.ViewObject.ShapeColor = (0.25, 0.55, 0.85)\nprint(f\"  Size:             {TOP_W}x{TOP_D}x{TOP_H}mm\")\nprint(f\"  Bearing pocket:   D{TOP_BEARING_POCKET_D}mm x {TOP_BEARING_POCKET_H}mm (SLIP fit)\")\nprint(f\"  Retaining lip:    natural shoulder at pocket bottom\")\nprint(f\"  Shaft bore:       D{SHAFT_CLEAR}mm\")\nprint(f\"  Volume:           {top.Volume:.0f}mm^3\")\n\n# =============================================================================\n# BUILD BOTTOM BLOCK (revised stack)\n# =============================================================================\nprint(f\"\\n[2/2] Building BOTTOM block...\")\n\nbot = Part.makeBox(BOT_W, BOT_D, BOT_H)\nbot.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(-BOT_W / 2.0, -BOT_D / 2.0, 0))\n\n# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Stack from BOTTOM to TOP:\n#   Z=0          - outside base\n#   Z=0 to 3     - solid PETG floor\n#   Z=3 to 4.5   - LOWER thrust washer pocket (steel washer, slip fit)\n#   Z=4.5 to 13.5 - 51101 thrust bearing pocket (slip fit)\n#   Z=13.5 to 15 - UPPER thrust washer pocket (steel washer)\n#   Z=15 to 23   - 6001-2RS radial bearing pocket (slip fit + Loctite)\n#   Z=23 to 35   - solid PETG top (thread engagement for optional inserts)\n# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nz_cursor = BOT_FLOOR_H  # Total: $24.</div>\\n\\n  <h3 style=\\\"color:#7e22ce;\\\">Item 1: Loctite 603 Retaining Compound</h3>\\n  <div class=\\\"product-card recommended\\\">\\n    <div class=\\\"prod-title\\\">Loctite 603 Threadlocker Oil-Tolerant Retaining Compound 10ml</div>\\n    <div class=\\\"prod-details\\\"><strong>Why this:</strong> The V2 design uses slip-fit bearings (0.05mm clearance) locked into place with Loctite 603. This is a high-strength retaining compound specifically designed for bearing installation on metal and plastic. Shear strength ~17 N/mm^2 after 24h cure. One 10ml bottle is enough for the entire project (each bearing uses ~0.2ml).</div>\\n    <div class=\\\"prod-details\\\"><strong>Amazon product:</strong> <span class=\\\"asin-code\\\">B000HBGVEY</span></div>\\n    <div class=\\\"prod-link\\\"><a href=\\\"https://www.amazon.com/dp/B000HBGVEY\\\">https://www.amazon.com/dp/B000HBGVEY</a></div>\\n    <div class=\\\"prod-details\\\"><strong>Search fallback:</strong> Amazon search \\\"Loctite 603 10ml\\\" or \\\"Loctite 603 retaining compound\\\"</div>\\n    <span class=\\\"price-tag\\\">$15-20</span>\\n    <div class=\\\"recommendation\\\">TIP: If Loctite 603 unavailable, Loctite 609 or Permatex 640 retaining compounds are equivalent. Avoid regular threadlockers (242/262) - those are for threads, not bearing retention.</div>\\n  </div>\\n\\n  <h3 style=\\\"color:#7e22ce; margin-top:25px;\\\">Item 2: Steel Thrust Washers</h3>\\n  <div class=\\\"product-card recommended\\\">\\n    <div class=\\\"prod-title\\\">Steel Thrust Washer 12mm ID x 26mm OD x 1.5mm thick (pack of 10 or more)</div>\\n    <div class=\\\"prod-details\\\"><strong>Why this:</strong> The 51101 thrust bearing must NOT rest directly on PETG - plastic will creep and deform under axial load. Steel washers above and below the thrust bearing distribute the load properly. Need 2 washers minimum, pack of 10 is cheap insurance.</div>\\n    <div class=\\\"prod-details\\\"><strong>Amazon product recommendation:</strong> <span class=\\\"asin-code\\\">B07P4L7NBD</span> or similar</div>\\n    <div class=\\\"prod-link\\\"><a href=\\\"https://www.amazon.com/s?k=thrust+washer+12mm+26mm\\\">Search: thrust washer 12mm 26mm</a></div>\\n    <div class=\\\"prod-details\\\"><strong>Search terms to use on Amazon:</strong> \\\"thrust washer 12mm 26mm 1.5mm\\\" or \\\"flat washer 12mm ID 26mm OD hardened steel\\\"</div>\\n    <div class=\\\"prod-details\\\"><strong>Required specs:</strong> ID exactly 12mm (shaft passes through), OD 26mm to match 51101 outer, thickness 1-2mm, material hardened carbon steel or stainless steel (NOT aluminum).</div>\\n    <span class=\\\"price-tag\\\">$5-8</span>\\n    <div class=\\\"recommendation\\\">TIP: McMaster-Carr part 92141A031 (12mm x 26mm x 1.5mm) is the professional option at ~$3 each. Amazon packs are cheaper for quantity.</div>\\n  </div>\\n\\n  <div class=\\\"alert alert-v2\\\" style=\\\"margin-top:20px;\\\">\\n    <div>\\n      <strong>Why both items are essential:</strong> Without Loctite 603, bearings will gradually rotate in their PETG pockets and create noise/wobble. Without thrust washers, the steel 51101 bearing will sink into the PETG over time (thermoplastic creep). Both failures take weeks to appear but are expensive to fix once assembled. Total cost $24 vs. reprinting the bearing housing later - an easy decision.\\n    </div>\\n  </div>\\n</div>\\n\\n<!-- ==================================================================== -->\\n<div class=\\\"section\\\">\\n  <h2>Section B - Already Ordered (41 items, $888.80)</h2>\\n  <div class=\\\"section-desc\\\">Full list of purchased items with verification status. Position the indicator tip against the shaft end\n3. Slowly rotate the shaft by hand\n4. The needle shows how much the shaft wobbles as it turns\n\n**Target specification:** Less than 0.2mm TIR (Total Indicator Reading) at the shaft end.\n\n## Why this matters for your CSM\n\nThe cylinder spins at 60-120 RPM with needles that must pass through cam zones at precise heights. If the shaft wobbles:\n\n| Wobble amount | Result |\n|---|---|\n| &lt;0.2mm | Machine runs smoothly, needles pass cleanly |\n| 0.2-0.5mm | Visible vibration, possible needle jams at high RPM |\n| &gt;0.5mm | Will fail - needles catch on cam edges, yarn breaks |\n\nWith a dial indicator you measure this directly. Without one, you can only tell \"does it look wobbly\" by eye - which catches wobble down to about 0.5mm at best.\n\n## When you'd check runout\n\n- **After bearing install** (before Loctite cures) - verify nothing is misaligned\n- **After Loctite cure** - confirm final alignment\n- **When something feels wrong** later - diagnose vibration issues\n\nSo in total, maybe 2-3 actual measurement sessions across the whole build.\n\n## Honest assessment - is it really necessary?\n\n### Arguments FOR having it\n\n1. **Prevents expensive mistakes.** If bearings are misaligned and you glue them with Loctite without checking, you'd have to destroy the printed blocks to fix it. A $38 tool vs $30+ of printed parts + 12 hours of reprinting.\n\n2. **Catches shaft defects early.** If FEYRINX sent you a slightly bent shaft, you need to know BEFORE installing bearings. Just rolling the shaft on a flat table catches bends down to ~0.5mm - the dial indicator catches 0.05mm.\n\n3. **Valuable for future projects.** If you build anything else with precision rotating parts (CNC, lathe attachments, other knitting machines), you'll use this tool constantly.\n\n4. **You already have a caliper** - that handles linear measurements. A dial indicator handles rotational/positional measurements. They're complementary tools.\n\n### Arguments AGAINST\n\n1. **For a prototype, \"good enough\" alignment works.** If your bearings feel smooth when you rotate the shaft by hand, and the cylinder doesn't visibly wobble when spinning, the machine will probably work fine for basic sock knitting.\n\n2. **Budget alternatives exist:**\n   - **V-block + eyeball** - Place shaft on two identical blocks, spin it, watch for wobble. Catches gross problems for $0.\n   - **DTI clamped to a wooden block** - Lower-precision test for ~$15.\n   - **Just feel it** - A badly-aligned shaft binds when you try to rotate it. A gross misalignment is obvious without tools.\n\n3. **For a DIY hobby machine**, industrial precision measurements are overkill. You're not running 8 hours/day at 200 RPM - you're knitting socks occasionally.\n\n## My honest recommendation\n\n**You probably don't NEED it for this project**, but it's a reasonable purchase because:\n\n- $38 is a small fraction of your $1,263 total spend\n- You'll use it for the actual measurement at least twice\n- It saves you from one potentially ruinous mistake (gluing misaligned bearings)\n- It's a permanent tool addition to your workshop\n\n### If you want to save money\n\nYou could return it and use alternative methods:\n\n1. **Roll test for shaft straightness** - free, catches major bends\n2. **Hand-feel test for bearings** - if it spins smoothly by finger pressure, alignment is good enough\n3. **Visual cylinder spin test** - if the cylinder wobbles less than a fingernail width when spinning, you're fine\n\n**Refund: $37.98**\n\n### If you keep it\n\nWhen you install the bearings, you'll actually measure shaft runout and have confidence that alignment is correct. The measurement takes 2 minutes. And you have a lifetime tool for future projects.\n\n## My personal vote\n\n**Keep it.** $38 for peace of mind on a $1,200 project is good insurance. And \"destructively remove Loctite-glued bearings\" is a miserable task - Loctite 603 holds at 12,000N.\n\nBut it's genuinely optional. If you want to save $38 and trust your hand feel for alignment, that's a defensible choice for a hobby machine.\n\n## Bottom line\n\nThe dial indicator is **nice to have, not must have** for this specific project. Applying Smalley's force-deflection equation P = (K\u00b7f\u00b7E\u00b7t\u00b3\u00b7N\u2074)/(Dm\u00b3\u00b7b) with E = 200 GPa for 17-7PH, t = 0.45 mm, N = 3 waves, mean diameter Dm = 18.5 mm, radial wall b = 6.5 mm, and f = 1 mm deflection yields roughly **25\u201335 N** \u2014 directly on target. Minibearings.com publishes data for a smaller 4 \u00d7 10 \u00d7 1.1 mm \u00d7 0.20 mm-thick 2-wave carbon-steel bearing preload washer at 30 N/mm spring rate; scaling geometry to your 12 \u00d7 25 \u00d7 ~2.5 mm \u00d7 0.4\u20130.5 mm thickness lands in the 25\u201340 N/mm range. Lisheng's LM-30 heavy variant (LM30-H1, 3.5 waves, 0.46 mm) delivers 37.9 N/mm, which with 1 mm deflection is 37.9 N \u2014 slightly over your window but within the 25\u201335 N acceptable band you specified. **Smalley's entire bearing-preload product family is specifically sized for 10\u2013100 N of preload on 6000-series bearings; 30 N is textbook.**\n\n## Cost summary and mistakes to avoid\n\n| Path | Wave spring | Spacer | Total | Timeline |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| Amazon-only (compromise) | B077S9DX92, ~$12 | B06W57V93L, ~$100 (stack 2) | ~$112 | 2\u20133 weeks |\n| McMaster-Carr (recommended) | Wave disc spring, ~$10 | 12\u00d718\u00d72 SS shim, ~$10 | ~$20 | Next day |\n| Enduro + McMaster (best) | WA Wave 12/0.3, ~$4 | 12\u00d718\u00d72 SS shim, ~$10 | ~$14 | 3\u20135 days |\n\n**Six shopping traps worth memorizing:** First, \"M12\" in washer/spring listings almost always means \"for an M12 bolt\" (13 mm ID), not \"12 mm ID\" \u2014 this single misunderstanding will waste most of your search time. Second, a **Belleville disc spring will look nearly identical in product photos but has ~10\u00d7 the spring rate of a wave spring**, so a 12\u00d725 Belleville will crush your bearing at 200+ N before you reach 0.5 mm compression. Third, single-turn stamped \"crinkle\" washers typically have only 0.8 mm free height and go solid at 0.5 mm deflection \u2014 you physically cannot get 1 mm of working travel out of them. Fourth, 65Mn carbon steel (standard on cheap Chinese springs) rusts in humid environments; specify 17-7PH or 302 stainless if your shop isn't climate-controlled. Fifth, verify the shim thickness is 2.0 mm and not 1.5 or 2.5 \u2014 a 0.5 mm stack-height error either over-preloads to seizure or leaves the stack rattling. Sixth, zinc-plated mild-steel washers are soft (~140 HV) and dish under concentrated thrust load; use hardened spring steel (DIN 988) or stainless for anything carrying axial preload.\n\n## Bottom line\n\nSpend $14 at Enduro Bearings plus McMaster-Carr and be done in a week, or spend $112 and three weeks routing a custom Lisheng order through Amazon. The Amazon-only path is technically feasible but gives you a compromised part (wrong ID or wrong thickness) at a worse price than the industrial-supply alternative. And before you order anything, correct the wave spring spec from \"multi-turn crest-to-crest\" to \"single-turn 3-wave disc washer, ~0.45 mm thick, 17-7PH\" \u2014 your 1 mm working window and 30 N target are inconsistent with the original multi-turn specification.",

assembly step:</strong> The preload collar positioning is what makes this work.\n    Follow exact Z-position specs for the shaft collars.\n  </div>\n\n  <h3 style=\"color:#86198f;\">Shaft Collar Positioning (from BOTTOM face of bottom block = Z=0)</h3>\n\n  <table style=\"max-width:800px;\">\n    <thead><tr><th>Component</th><th>Z Position (mm)</th><th>Purpose</th></tr></thead>\n    <tbody>\n      <tr><td><strong>Bottom shaft collar</strong></td><td>Z = -2mm</td><td>Just below block, acts as hard stop</td></tr>\n      <tr><td>Bottom block bottom face</td><td>Z = 0</td><td>Reference plane</td></tr>\n      <tr><td>Bottom block top face</td><td>Z = 35mm</td><td>Bottom housing boundary</td></tr>\n      <tr><td>Gap between blocks</td><td>Z = 35 to 40mm</td><td>5mm aluminum plate mount</td></tr>\n      <tr><td>Top block bottom face</td><td>Z = 40mm</td><td>Top housing starts</td></tr>\n      <tr><td>Top block top face</td><td>Z = 60mm</td><td>Top housing ends</td></tr>\n      <tr><td><strong>Top collar NEUTRAL (touching)</strong></td><td>Z = 60mm</td><td>Just touches top bearing, no preload</td></tr>\n      <tr><td><strong>Top collar WORKING (preloaded)</strong></td><td>Z = 59mm</td><td>1mm compression = ~30N preload</td></tr>\n    </tbody>\n  </table>\n\n  <h3 style=\"color:#86198f; margin-top:20px;\">Assembly Sequence (follow in order)</h3>\n\n  <ol style=\"margin-left: 20px; line-height: 1.8;\">\n    <li>Print both bearing housing blocks (V2.3 STL from macro)</li>\n    <li>Clean bearing pockets with IPA, apply Loctite 603 for 51101 thrust bearing</li>\n    <li>Press 51101 thrust bearing onto lower 2x AS1226 washers (in floor pocket)</li>\n    <li>Place upper 2x AS1226 washers above thrust bearing</li>\n    <li>Drop wave spring into spring pocket (sits loosely at free height)</li>\n    <li>Place spacer ring on top of wave spring</li>\n    <li>Apply Loctite 603, install 6001-2RS radial bearing in bottom block</li>\n    <li>Apply Loctite 603, install 6001-2RS radial bearing in top block</li>\n    <li><strong>Cure Loctite 24 hours at room temperature</strong></li>\n    <li>Mount bottom housing to aluminum plate with M5 flathead screws</li>\n    <li>Install bottom shaft collar at Z = -2mm (clamp tight)</li>\n    <li>Insert shaft through bottom housing, through spring/spacer, through radial bearing</li>\n    <li>Insert shaft through top bearing in top housing</li>\n    <li>Slide top shaft collar down until it just touches top bearing (Z=60mm)</li>\n    <li><strong>Push shaft DOWN 1mm firmly, then tighten top collar at Z=59mm</strong></li>\n    <li>Final check: shaft spins freely, NO click, NO axial play</li>\n  </ol>\n\n  <h3 style=\"color:#86198f; margin-top:20px;\">Preload Tuning</h3>\n  <ul style=\"margin-left: 20px;\">\n    <li><strong>Too loose</strong> (hear click or feel play): Loosen top collar, move DOWN 0.2-0.3mm, retighten</li>\n    <li><strong>Too tight</strong> (rotation feels heavy): Loosen top collar, move UP 0.2mm, retighten</li>\n    <li><strong>Correct</strong>: Shaft spins smoothly, zero click, zero axial play</li>\n  </ul>\n\n  <div class=\"alert alert-info\">\n    <strong>Pro tip:</strong> Mark a reference line on the shaft at Z=59mm from bottom face with a marker pen.\n    Makes re-assembly repeatable every time without re-measuring.\n  </div>\n</div>\n\n<!-- ==================================================================== -->\\n<div class=\\\"section\\\">\\n  <h2>V2.3 Assembly Process (IMPORTANT)</h2>\\n\\n  <div class=\\\"alert alert-v23\\\">\\n    <strong>New assembly step:</strong> The preload collar positioning is what makes this work.\\n    Follow exact Z-position specs for the shaft collars.\\n  </div>\\n\\n  <h3 style=\\\"color:#86198f;\\\">Shaft Collar Positioning (from BOTTOM face of bottom block = Z=0)</h3>\\n\\n  <table style=\\\"max-width:800px;\\\">\\n    <thead><tr><th>Component</th><th>Z Position (mm)</th><th>Purpose</th></tr></thead>\\n    <tbody>\\n      <tr><td><strong>Bottom shaft collar</strong></td><td>Z = -2mm</td><td>Just below block, acts as hard stop</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td>Bottom block bottom face</td><td>Z = 0</td><td>Reference plane</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td>Bottom block top face</td><td>Z = 35mm</td><td>Bottom housing boundary</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td>Gap between blocks</td><td>Z = 35 to 40mm</td><td>5mm aluminum plate mount</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td>Top block bottom face</td><td>Z = 40mm</td><td>Top housing starts</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td>Top block top face</td><td>Z = 60mm</td><td>Top housing ends</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td><strong>Top collar NEUTRAL (touching)</strong></td><td>Z = 60mm</td><td>Just touches top bearing, no preload</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td><strong>Top collar WORKING (preloaded)</strong></td><td>Z = 59mm</td><td>1mm compression = ~30N preload</td></tr>\\n    </tbody>\\n  </table>\\n\\n  <h3 style=\\\"color:#86198f; margin-top:20px;\\\">Assembly Sequence (follow in order)</h3>\\n\\n  <ol style=\\\"margin-left: 20px; line-height: 1.8;\\\">\\n    <li>Print both bearing housing blocks (V2.3 STL from macro)</li>\\n    <li>Clean bearing pockets with IPA, apply Loctite 603 for 51101 thrust bearing</li>\\n    <li>Press 51101 thrust bearing onto lower 2x AS1226 washers (in floor pocket)</li>\\n    <li>Place upper 2x AS1226 washers above thrust bearing</li>\\n    <li>Drop wave spring into spring pocket (sits loosely at free height)</li>\\n    <li>Place spacer ring on top of wave spring</li>\\n    <li>Apply Loctite 603, install 6001-2RS radial bearing in bottom block</li>\\n    <li>Apply Loctite 603, install 6001-2RS radial bearing in top block</li>\\n    <li><strong>Cure Loctite 24 hours at room temperature</strong></li>\\n    <li>Mount bottom housing to aluminum plate with M5 flathead screws</li>\\n    <li>Install bottom shaft collar at Z = -2mm (clamp tight)</li>\\n    <li>Insert shaft through bottom housing, through spring/spacer, through radial bearing</li>\\n    <li>Insert shaft through top bearing in top housing</li>\\n    <li>Slide top shaft collar down until it just touches top bearing (Z=60mm)</li>\\n    <li><strong>Push shaft DOWN 1mm firmly, then tighten top collar at Z=59mm</strong></li>\\n    <li>Final check: shaft spins freely, NO click, NO axial play</li>\\n  </ol>\\n\\n  <h3 style=\\\"color:#86198f; margin-top:20px;\\\">Preload Tuning</h3>\\n  <ul style=\\\"margin-left: 20px;\\\">\\n    <li><strong>Too loose</strong> (hear click or feel play): Loosen top collar, move DOWN 0.2-0.3mm, retighten</li>\\n    <li><strong>Too tight</strong> (rotation feels heavy): Loosen top collar, move UP 0.2mm, retighten</li>\\n    <li><strong>Correct</strong>: Shaft spins smoothly, zero click, zero axial play</li>\\n  </ul>\\n\\n  <div class=\\\"alert alert-info\\\">\\n    <strong>Pro tip:</strong> Mark a reference line on the shaft at Z=59mm from bottom face with a marker pen.\\n    Makes re-assembly repeatable every time without re-measuring.\\n  </div>\\n</div>\\n\\n<!-- ==================================================================== -->\\n<div line-height: 1.8;\">\n    <li>Print all 3 STLs from V2.4 macro (top block, bottom block, spacer tube)</li>\n    <li>Apply Loctite 603 to bearing pockets, install:\n      <ul>\n        <li>51101 thrust bearing in bottom block lower pocket</li>\n        <li>6001-2RS radial bearing in bottom block upper pocket</li>\n        <li>6001-2RS radial bearing in top block</li>\n      </ul>\n    </li>\n    <li>Cure Loctite 24 hours at room temperature</li>\n    <li>In bottom block, stack: lower 2x AS1226 washers \u2192 wave spring \u2192 spacer ring (no Loctite on spring/spacer/washers)</li>\n    <li>Mount bottom block to aluminum plate using M5 flathead screws</li>\n    <li>Mount top block to a separate plate using M5 flathead screws</li>\n    <li>Verify 11mm gap between blocks (use spacer tube as gauge - it should JUST barely touch both bearing inner races when unloaded)</li>\n    <li>Install bottom shaft collar at Z = -2mm (clamped tightly)</li>\n    <li>Insert shaft through bottom block</li>\n    <li><strong>Slide spacer tube onto shaft</strong> (sits on bottom radial bearing inner race)</li>\n    <li>Lower top block onto shaft (top bearing slides over shaft, contacts top of spacer tube)</li>\n    <li>Bolt top plate to frame (this defines block gap)</li>\n    <li>Install top shaft collar - <strong>LIGHTLY clamp (retention only, no compression force)</strong></li>\n  </ol>\n\n  <h3 style=\"color:#1e40af;\">Test Protocol (Verify Preload Works)</h3>\n  <ol style=\"margin-left: 20px;\">\n    <li><strong>Rotation test:</strong> Spin shaft by hand. Should feel smooth with slight resistance.</li>\n    <li><strong>Axial play test:</strong> Try to lift/push shaft. Should be ZERO movement.</li>\n    <li><strong>Click test:</strong> Rotate slowly listening for clicks. Should be silent.</li>\n    <li><strong>Drag test:</strong> Spin shaft, time to coastdown. Should rotate freely 5+ seconds.</li>\n    <li><strong>Runout test:</strong> Use dial indicator. <0.2mm TIR at shaft end.</li>\n    <li><strong>Heat test:</strong> Run 30 RPM for 10 minutes. Industrial standard.</div>\\n    <span class=\\\"price-tag\\\">$15-30</span>\\n  </div>\\n\\n  <h3 style=\\\"color:#1e40af;\\\">Optional: Shim Kit for Fine-Tuning Preload</h3>\\n\\n  <div class=\\\"product-card recommended\\\">\\n    <div class=\\\"prod-title\\\">Mixed thickness shim washer kit (12mm ID)</div>\\n    <div class=\\\"prod-details\\\"><strong>Specs:</strong> 12mm ID x 18mm OD x various thicknesses (0.1, 0.2, 0.3mm)</div>\\n    <div class=\\\"prod-details\\\"><strong>Why useful:</strong> If first assembly is too tight or too loose, slip a shim above/below the spring to adjust preload by ~5N per 0.1mm.
