Assembly is simpler and more repeatable.\\n  </div>\\n\\n  <h3 style=\\\"color:#1e40af;\\\">Block Gap Verification (CRITICAL)</h3>\\n  <div class=\\\"action-required\\\">\\n    <h3>Block gap MUST be 11mm</h3>\\n    <p>The spacer tube length (29.40mm) was calculated based on:</p>\\n    <ul style=\\\"margin: 5px 0 5px 20px;\\\">\\n      <li>6mm aluminum mounting plate</li>\\n      <li>5mm assembly clearance (for fasteners and access)</li>\\n      <li><strong>Total: 11mm gap between top of bottom block and bottom of top block</strong></li>\\n    </ul>\\n    <p><strong>If your actual block gap differs from 11mm, recalculate the spacer length:</strong></p>\\n    <p style=\\\"font-family: monospace; background: #fff; padding: 8px; border-radius: 4px;\\\">\\n      Spacer length = (Block gap) + 18.4mm\\n    </p>\\n    <p>Examples: gap = 10mm \\u2192 spacer 28.4mm. gap = 12mm \\u2192 spacer 30.4mm.</p>\\n  </div>\\n\\n  <h3 style=\\\"color:#1e40af;\\\">Step-by-step Assembly</h3>\\n  <ol style=\\\"margin-left: 20px; line-height: 1.8;\\\">\\n    <li>Print all 3 STLs from V2.4 macro (top block, bottom block, spacer tube)</li>\\n    <li>Apply Loctite 603 to bearing pockets, install:\\n      <ul>\\n        <li>51101 thrust bearing in bottom block lower pocket</li>\\n        <li>6001-2RS radial bearing in bottom block upper pocket</li>\\n        <li>6001-2RS radial bearing in top block</li>\\n      </ul>\\n    </li>\\n    <li>Cure Loctite 24 hours at room temperature</li>\\n    <li>In bottom block, stack: lower 2x AS1226 washers \\u2192 wave spring \\u2192 spacer ring (no Loctite on spring/spacer/washers)</li>\\n    <li>Mount bottom block to aluminum plate using M5 flathead screws</li>\\n    <li>Mount top block to a separate plate using M5 flathead screws</li>\\n    <li>Verify 11mm gap between blocks (use spacer tube as gauge - it should JUST barely touch both bearing inner races when unloaded)</li>\\n    <li>Install bottom shaft collar at Z = -2mm (clamped tightly)</li>\\n    <li>Insert shaft through bottom block</li>\\n    <li><strong>Slide spacer tube onto shaft</strong> (sits on bottom radial bearing inner race)</li>\\n    <li>Lower top block onto shaft (top bearing slides over shaft, contacts top of spacer tube)</li>\\n    <li>Bolt top plate to frame (this defines block gap)</li>\\n    <li>Install top shaft collar - <strong>LIGHTLY clamp (retention only, no compression force)</strong></li>\\n  </ol>\\n\\n  <h3 style=\\\"color:#1e40af;\\\">Test Protocol (Verify Preload Works)</h3>\\n  <ol style=\\\"margin-left: 20px;\\\">\\n    <li><strong>Rotation test:</strong> Spin shaft by hand. Should feel smooth with slight resistance.</li>\\n    <li><strong>Axial play test:</strong> Try to lift/push shaft. Should be ZERO movement.</li>\\n    <li><strong>Click test:</strong> Rotate slowly listening for clicks. Should be silent.</li>\\n    <li><strong>Drag test:</strong> Spin shaft, time to coastdown. Should rotate freely 5+ seconds.</li>\\n    <li><strong>Runout test:</strong> Use dial indicator. <0.2mm TIR at shaft end.</li>\\n    <li><strong>Heat test:</strong> Run 30 RPM for 10 minutes. Should remain cool to touch.</li>\\n  </ol>\\n\\n  <h3 style=\\\"color:#1e40af;\\\">Fine-Tuning (if any test fails)</h3>\\n  <table>\\n    <thead><tr><th>Symptom</th><th>Cause</th><th>Fix</th></tr></thead>\\n    <tbody>\\n      <tr><td>Click/rattle on rotation</td><td>Spacer tube too LONG (insufficient preload)</td><td>Shorten spacer 0.1-0.2mm OR remove a shim from the wave spring stack</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td>Heavy drag, stiff rotation</td><td>Spacer tube too SHORT (excessive preload)</td><td>Add 0.1mm shim above the spacer ring</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td>Heat buildup</td><td>Excessive preload</td><td>Same as above - reduce preload</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td>Axial play (~0.1-0.5mm)</td><td>Spacer too long OR spring damaged</td><td>Shorten spacer; inspect spring for plastic deformation</td></tr>\\n    </tbody>\\n  </table>\\n</div>\\n\\n<!-- ==================================================================== -->\\n<div class=\\\"section\\\">\\n  <h2>Section 1 - All 57 Existing Orders (Status Unchanged)</h2>\\n  <div class=\\\"alert alert-success\\\">\\n    <strong>All 57 existing orders remain valid.</strong> V2.4 is purely additive - no existing parts need to be returned or replaced. The \"drive hub\" is a printed part that sits **above the pulley**, clamps to the shaft, and has **4 bolts going UP into the cassette base** (not into the pulley).\n\n**Function:**\n```\nCassette base (above)\n   |\n   | <- 4x M5 bolts from drive hub UP into cassette\n   |\n[Drive Hub] (12mm clamp on shaft)\n   |\n   | <- 60T pulley on shaft below, with own set screw\n   |\n[60T HTD 5M pulley]\n```\n\n**Pros:**\n- Uses your existing pulley as-is (no drilling)\n- Drive hub is purely a printed part\n- Standard architecture in industrial CSM machines\n\n**Cons:**\n- More vertical stack height\n- Two clamping points on shaft (pulley + hub)\n\n### Path B: Drive hub REPLACES the pulley's hub interface\n**What it does:** You drill 4 holes through the 60T pulley flange. # Chamfer outer edges of body, flange, boss (skip inner edges near shaft)\n            if r1 > 8.0:  # skip shaft bore edges\n                edges_to_chamfer.append(edge)\n    if edges_to_chamfer:\n Center boss (concentricity feature on top of flange)\\nboss = Part.makeCylinder(BOSS_OD / 2.0, BOSS_H)\\nboss.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, TOTAL_H))\\n\\n# 4. Combine into single solid\\nhub = body.fuse(flange).fuse(boss)\\n\\n# 5. Shaft bore through entire hub (12.1mm slip fit)\\nshaft_bore = Part.makeCylinder(SHAFT_BORE / 2.0, TOTAL_H + BOSS_H + 2)\\nshaft_bore.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, -1))\\nhub = hub.cut(shaft_bore)\\n\\n# 6. Clamp slot (vertical slot from one side, through clamp section only)\\n# Slot extends from outer edge through to past shaft, allowing clamp action\\nslot_w = CLAMP_SLOT_W\\nslot_h = HUB_BODY_H + 0.1  # slightly above body section\\n# Slot starts from outer edge of hub body (Y = HUB_BODY_OD/2)\\n# Cuts inward toward shaft, stops 6mm short of shaft for material bridge\\nslot = Part.makeBox(slot_w, HUB_BODY_OD / 2.0 + 1.0, slot_h)\\nslot.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(-slot_w / 2.0, 0, 0))  # centered on Y axis, extends +Y\\nhub = hub.cut(slot)\\n\\n# 7. Clamp bolts - 2x M5 horizontal, perpendicular to slot\\n# Bolts thread along Y axis, pulling clamp closed\\n# Bolt path: from -Y side (head) through slot to +Y side (nut pocket)\\nfor z_pos in [CLAMP_BOLT_Z1, CLAMP_BOLT_Z2]:\\n    # M5 clearance through-hole along Y axis\\n    bolt_hole = Part.makeCylinder(CLAMP_BOLT_D / 2.0, HUB_BODY_OD + 4)\\n    bolt_hole.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, 0), FreeCAD.Vector(1, 0, 0), 90)  # rotate to Y axis\\n    bolt_hole.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, -HUB_BODY_OD / 2.0 - 2, z_pos))\\n    hub = hub.cut(bolt_hole)\\n\\n    # Socket head pocket on -Y side (bolt head)\\n    head_pocket = Part.makeCylinder(CLAMP_BOLT_HEAD_D / 2.0, CLAMP_BOLT_HEAD_H + 2)\\n    head_pocket.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, 0), FreeCAD.Vector(1, 0, 0), 90)\\n    head_pocket.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, -HUB_BODY_OD / 2.0 - 2, z_pos))\\n    hub = hub.cut(head_pocket)\\n\\n    # M5 hex nut pocket on +Y side (captures nut, prevents rotation)\\n    nut_pocket = hex_prism(CLAMP_NUT_FLAT + 0.3, CLAMP_NUT_H + 1.0)\\n    nut_pocket.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, 0), FreeCAD.Vector(1, 0, 0), -90)\\n    nut_pocket.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, HUB_BODY_OD / 2.0 - CLAMP_NUT_H - 1.0, z_pos))\\n    hub = hub.cut(nut_pocket)\\n\\n# 8. Cassette mount bolts (4x M5 flathead, threading UP from below into cassette inserts)\\n# Bolt heads sit FLUSH on bottom face of flange (countersink on flange bottom)\\n# Through-holes pass through flange thickness\\nfor i in range(CASSETTE_BOLT_COUNT):\\n    ang = math.radians(i * 360.0 / CASSETTE_BOLT_COUNT + 45.0)  # offset by 45 deg\\n    bx = (CASSETTE_BOLT_PCD / 2.0) * math.cos(ang)\\n    by = (CASSETTE_BOLT_PCD / 2.0) * math.sin(ang)\\n\\n    # Through-hole for M5 shank\\n    bh = Part.makeCylinder(CASSETTE_BOLT_D / 2.0, FLANGE_H + 2)\\n    bh.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(bx, by, HUB_BODY_H - 1))\\n    hub = hub.cut(bh)\\n\\n    # 90 degree countersink on BOTTOM of flange (head sits flush from below)\\n    csk = make_csk_cone(CSK_TOP_D / 2.0, CASSETTE_BOLT_D / 2.0, CSK_DEPTH)\\n    csk.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(bx, by, HUB_BODY_H))\\n    hub = hub.cut(csk)\\n\\n# 9. Apply chamfer to outer edges (top of flange + top of boss + bottom of body)\\ntry:\\n    edges_to_chamfer = []\\n    for edge in hub.Edges:\\n        v1, v2 = edge.Vertexes[0].Point, edge.Vertexes[1].Point\\n        # Horizontal circular edges only (top/bottom of cylindrical features)\\n        if abs(v1.z - v2.z) < 0.01:\\n            r1 = (v1.x ** 2 + v1.y ** 2) ** 0.5\\n            # Chamfer outer edges of body, flange, boss (skip inner edges near shaft)\\n            if r1 > 8.0:  # skip shaft bore edges\\n                edges_to_chamfer.append(edge)\\n    if edges_to_chamfer:\\n        hub = hub.makeChamfer(CHAMFER_SIZE, edges_to_chamfer)\\nexcept Exception as e:\\n    print(f\\\"  Chamfer warning: {e}\\\")\\n\\n# Add to document\\nobj_hub = doc.addObject(\\\"Part::Feature\\\", \\\"DriveHub_V2_4\\\")\\nobj_hub.Shape = hub\\nobj_hub.ViewObject.ShapeColor = (0.85, 0.65, 0.25)  # gold/brass tone\\nprint(f\\\"  Hub body OD:       {HUB_BODY_OD}mm\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  Hub body height:   {HUB_BODY_H}mm\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  Flange OD:         {FLANGE_OD}mm\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  Flange thickness:  {FLANGE_H}mm\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  Center boss:       D{BOSS_OD}mm x {BOSS_H}mm tall\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  Total height:      {TOTAL_H + BOSS_H}mm\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  Shaft bore:        D{SHAFT_BORE}mm\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  Clamp bolts:       2x M5 at Z={CLAMP_BOLT_Z1}, {CLAMP_BOLT_Z2}mm\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  Cassette bolts:    {CASSETTE_BOLT_COUNT}x M5 PCD {CASSETTE_BOLT_PCD}mm\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  Volume:            {hub.Volume:.0f}mm^3\\\")\\n\\ndoc.recompute()\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# EXPORT STL\\n# Fuse plate and foot into L-bracket\\nbracket = plate.fuse(foot)\\n\\n# 4. Cut motor pilot boss clearance hole (center of plate, axis=X)\\npilot_hole = Part.makeCylinder(PILOT_HOLE_D / 2.0, PLATE_T + 4)\\npilot_hole.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,1,0), 90)  # rotate to X axis\\npilot_hole.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(-2, 0, PLATE_H / 2.0))\\nbracket = bracket.cut(pilot_hole)\\n\\n# 5. Cut 4x motor mount holes (M5 at 47mm PCD around plate center)\\nplate_center_z = PLATE_H / 2.0\\nfor i in range(4):\\n    ang = math.radians(i * 90.0 + 45.0)\\n    by = (MOTOR_PCD / 2.0) * math.cos(ang)\\n    bz = (MOTOR_PCD / 2.0) * math.sin(ang) + plate_center_z\\n\\n    # Through-hole for M5 shank\\n    hole = Part.makeCylinder(MOTOR_BOLT_D / 2.0, PLATE_T + 4)\\n    hole.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,1,0), 90)\\n    hole.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(-2, by, bz))\\n    bracket = bracket.cut(hole)\\n\\n    # Counterbore for socket head (head sits flush from outside)\\n    head_pocket = Part.makeCylinder(MOTOR_BOLT_CSK_D / 2.0, MOTOR_BOLT_CSK_H + 1)\\n    head_pocket.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0,0,0), FreeCAD.Vector(0,1,0), 90)\\n    # Outside face is at X=PLATE_T, so head pocket starts there going outward\\n    head_pocket.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(PLATE_T - MOTOR_BOLT_CSK_H, by, bz))\\n    bracket = bracket.cut(head_pocket)\\n\\nprint(f\\\"  Motor face plate:     {PLATE_W}x{PLATE_H}x{PLATE_T}mm\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  Pilot hole:           D{PILOT_HOLE_D}mm\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  4x M5 holes at PCD:   {MOTOR_PCD}mm with counterbore D{MOTOR_BOLT_CSK_D}\\\")\\n\\n# 6. Cut 4x slotted holes in foot (for T-nut sliding belt tension adjust)\\n# Slots run along X direction (belt tension axis)\\n# Two pairs at Y = +/- FOOT_SLOT_SPACING_Y/2\\nfoot_top_z = -0.001  # just into foot top\\nslot_centers_y = [-FOOT_SLOT_SPACING_Y/2, FOOT_SLOT_SPACING_Y/2]\\nslot_centers_x = [FOOT_SLOT_PCD_X, FOOT_D - FOOT_SLOT_PCD_X]\\n\\nfor sx in slot_centers_x:\\n    for sy in slot_centers_y:\\n        # Slot through-hole\\n        slot = make_slot_hole(FOOT_BOLT_D, FOOT_SLOT_LEN, FOOT_T + 4)\\n        slot.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(sx, sy, -FOOT_T - 2))\\n        bracket = bracket.cut(slot)\\n\\n        # Counterbore for M5 socket head on top of foot\\n        head_slot = make_slot_hole(FOOT_SLOT_HEAD_D, FOOT_SLOT_LEN, FOOT_SLOT_HEAD_H + 1)\\n        head_slot.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(sx, sy, -FOOT_SLOT_HEAD_H))\\n        bracket = bracket.cut(head_slot)\\n\\nprint(f\\\"  Foot:                 {FOOT_W}x{FOOT_D}x{FOOT_T}mm\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  4x slotted holes:     {FOOT_SLOT_LEN}mm long, M5\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  Slot pattern:         {FOOT_SLOT_SPACING_Y}mm Y spacing\\\")\\n\\n# 7. Add reinforcement ribs (triangular, span the L-corner)\\n# Ribs are vertical triangles in the X-Z plane, distributed along Y\\nrib_y_spacing = (PLATE_W - 20) / (RIB_COUNT - 1) if RIB_COUNT > 1 else 0\\nrib_y_start = -(PLATE_W - 20) / 2.0\\nfor i in range(RIB_COUNT):\\n    rib_y = rib_y_start + i * rib_y_spacing if RIB_COUNT > 1 else 0\\n\\n    # Triangular rib: vertices at (PLATE_T, y, 0), (PLATE_T, y, RIB_HEIGHT), (PLATE_T+RIB_DEPTH, y, 0)\\n    # Actually we need the rib to attach to plate (X=PLATE_T side) and foot (top of foot, Z=0)\\n    pts = [\\n        FreeCAD.Vector(PLATE_T, rib_y - RIB_T/2.0, 0),\\n        FreeCAD.Vector(PLATE_T, rib_y - RIB_T/2.0, RIB_HEIGHT),\\n        FreeCAD.Vector(PLATE_T + RIB_DEPTH, rib_y - RIB_T/2.0, 0),\\n        FreeCAD.Vector(PLATE_T, rib_y - RIB_T/2.0, 0),  # close\\n    ]\\n    poly = Part.makePolygon(pts)\\n    face = Part.Face(Part.Wire(poly))\\n    rib = face.extrude(FreeCAD.Vector(0, RIB_T, 0))\\n    bracket = bracket.fuse(rib)\\n\\nprint(f\\\"  Ribs:                 {RIB_COUNT}x triangular, {RIB_T}mm thick\\\")\\n\\n# 8. Apply chamfer to outer edges (using V1.3 lessons - careful filter)\\ntry:\\n    edges_to_chamfer = []\\n    bb = bracket.BoundBox\\n    tol = 0.5\\n    for edge in bracket.Edges:\\n        v1, v2 = edge.Vertexes[0].Point, edge.Vertexes[1].Point\\n        # Only chamfer edges on the EXTREME outer surfaces of the bounding box\\n        # (skip all internal pocket/hole edges)\\n        on_boundary = False\\n        # Check if both endpoints are on a bounding box face\\n        for bx in [bb.XMin, bb.XMax]:\\n            if abs(v1.x - bx) < tol and abs(v2.x - bx) < tol:\\n                on_boundary = True\\n                break\\n        if not on_boundary:\\n            for by in [bb.YMin, bb.YMax]:\\n                if abs(v1.y - by) < tol and abs(v2.y - by) < tol:\\n                    on_boundary = True\\n                    break\\n        if not on_boundary:\\n            for bz in [bb.ZMin, bb.ZMax]:\\n                if abs(v1.z - bz) < tol and abs(v2.z - bz) < tol:\\n                    on_boundary = True\\n                    break\\n        # Also skip very short edges (likely artifacts of fillet/intersection)\\n        if on_boundary and edge.Length > 5.0:\\n            edges_to_chamfer.append(edge)\\n\\n    if edges_to_chamfer:\\n        bracket = bracket.makeChamfer(CHAMFER_SIZE, edges_to_chamfer)\\n        print(f\\\"  Chamfered:            {len(edges_to_chamfer)} outer edges\\\")\\nexcept Exception as e:\\n    print(f\\\"  Chamfer warning:      {e}\\\")\\n\\n# Add to document\\nobj_mount = doc.addObject(\\\"Part::Feature\\\", \\\"MotorMount_V1_0\\\")\\nobj_mount.Shape = bracket\\nobj_mount.ViewObject.ShapeColor = (0.6, 0.7, 0.8)  # blue-gray (industrial look)\\n\\nprint(f\\\"\\\\n  Total bounding box:   {bracket.BoundBox.XLength:.0f} x {bracket.BoundBox.YLength:.0f} x {bracket.BoundBox.ZLength:.0f}mm\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  Volume:               {bracket.Volume:.0f}mm^3\\\")\\nprint(f\\\"  Estimated weight:     {bracket.Volume * 1.27 / 1000:.0f}g (PETG, 50% infill)\\\")\\n\\ndoc.recompute()\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# EXPORT STL\\n# =============================================================================\\nprint(f\\\"\\\\nExporting STL...\\\")\\ntry:\\n    Part.export([obj_mount], PATH_STL)\\n    print(f\\\"  [OK] STL: {PATH_STL}\\\")\\nexcept Exception as e:\\n    print(f\\\"  [FAIL] STL: {e}\\\")\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# EXPORT PNG\\n# =============================================================================\\nprint(f\\\"\\\\nExporting PNG view...\\\")\\ntry:\\n    view = FreeCADGui.activeDocument().activeView()\\n    view.viewIsometric()\\n    view.fitAll()\\n    view.saveImage(PATH_PNG, 1600, 1200, \\\"Current\\\")\\n    print(f\\\"  [OK] PNG: {PATH_PNG}\\\")\\nexcept Exception as e:\\n    print(f\\\"  [WARN] PNG skipped: {e}\\\")\\n\\n# =============================================================================\\n# EXPORT SVG BLUEPRINT\\n# =============================================================================\\nprint(f\\\"\\\\nGenerating SVG blueprint...\\\")\\n\\nsvg_content = '''<svg viewBox=\\\"0 0 1100 800\\\" xmlns=\\\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\\\" font-family=\\\"Arial, sans-serif\\\">\\n  <rect width=\\\"1100\\\" height=\\\"800\\\" fill=\\\"#fafaf8\\\"/>\\n\\n  <text x=\\\"550\\\" y=\\\"32\\\" text-anchor=\\\"middle\\\" fill=\\\"#1a1a1a\\\" font-size=\\\"18\\\" font-weight=\\\"bold\\\">NEMA 23 MOTOR MOUNT V1.0 -- BLUEPRINT</text>\\n  <text x=\\\"550\\\" y=\\\"50\\\" text-anchor=\\\"middle\\\" fill=\\\"#666\\\" font-size=\\\"11\\\">L-bracket. At each slot END center, subtract a 90-degree chamfer cone\\n     - Cone matches semicircle radius at top of foot\\n     - Cone tapers inward as it goes down by the chamfer amount\\n     - This rounds the top edge of the slot end region\\n\\nThis addresses crack initiation at slot ends specifically, where\\nthe bolt repeatedly presses during tightening cycles.\\n\\nMath:\\n  M5 slot end radius: 2.75mm (half of slot width 5.5mm)\\n  Chamfer 0.8mm: cone goes from r=2.75 at top to r=2.0 at 0.8mm down\\n  This creates a 0.8mm chamfer on the slot end perimeter\\n\\nCode outline:\\n\\ndef make_slot_hole_with_relief(slot_w, slot_l, depth, end_relief=0.8):\\n    # Standard capsule slot\\n    radius = slot_w / 2.0\\n    rect_l = slot_l - slot_w\\n    rect = Part.makeBox(rect_l, slot_w, depth)\\n    rect.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(-rect_l/2.0, -slot_w/2.0, 0))\\n    cyl1 = Part.makeCylinder(radius, depth)\\n    cyl1.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(-rect_l/2.0, 0, 0))\\n    cyl2 = Part.makeCylinder(radius, depth)\\n    cyl2.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(rect_l/2.0, 0, 0))\\n    slot = rect.fuse(cyl1).fuse(cyl2)\\n\\n    # Add chamfer cones at slot ends (top of slot only)\\n    if end_relief > 0:\\n        for x_pos in [-rect_l/2.0, rect_l/2.0]:\\n            # Cone goes from full radius at top to (radius - end_relief) below\\n            cone = Part.makeCone(radius + 0.1,\\n                                 radius - end_relief,\\n                                 end_relief)\\n            cone.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(x_pos, 0, depth - end_relief))\\n            slot = slot.fuse(cone)\\n    return slot\\n\\n\\nWait - I'm subtracting from a hole. The hole is the CUT shape.\\nIf I FUSE a cone to the hole, the cone EXPANDS the hole at the top.\\nThat means more material is removed at the top -> chamfered upper edge.\\n\\nActually I want the OPPOSITE: chamfer the TOP edge of the hole.\\nTo chamfer the top edge OUTWARD: hole gets WIDER at the top.\\nThat means the hole shape itself needs to be a flared cylinder near the top.\\n\\nYes - the cone fused to the hole gives a wider opening at top = chamfered edge.\\nThis is correct.\\n\",\"stderr\":\"\"}"

        "text": "For Overlap Type Wave Springs and multiple turn Spirawaves, the radial wall must be sufficient to prevent misalignment between adjacent layers. For springs with a narrow radial wall, radial misalignment can occur during handling or during operation if the spring is not contained or closely piloted. Solutions to this problem include dimensioning the spring to pilot closely on the I.D. and/or O.D. or designing the spring as a single turn Gap Type. For springs that pilot on a shaft, the inside diameter can be toleranced to provide a minimum clearance from the shaft. Since wave springs expand during compression, interference with the shaft is generally not a concern. For springs that pilot in the bore, the bore and shaft diameters should be included in the spring specifications. The actual spring diameter is then developed at time of manufacture to provide the best fit and prevent binding due to expansion.\n\nStandard Springs vs Custom Springs Finding the right spring can be as easy as selecting a standard catalog item. A Smalley engineer can help you choose from over 4000 standard parts available from stock in carbon and stainless steel. Smalley\u2019s edgewinding manufacturing provides the utmost in flexibility and quality. Whether the requirement is for one spring or one million, consider Smalley for your special spring requirements. Defining the Spring Requirements Although wave spring applications are extremely diverse, there is a consistently basic set of rules for defining spring requirements.\n\nAlthough wave spring applications are extremely diverse, there is a consistently basic set of rules for defining spring requirements. Those requirements are used to select a stock/standard spring or design a special spring to meet the specifications. The working cavity usually consists of a bore the spring operates in and/or a shaft the spring clears. The spring stays positioned by piloting in the bore or on the shaft. The distance between the loading surfaces defines the axial working cavity or work height of the spring. Material cross-section plays an important role in wave spring design. The most economical materials are those used in manufacturing Smalley standard springs and retaining rings. In addition, many other material cross sections are commonly used in special spring manufacture designs. Smalley engineering can provide assistance in selecting an economical alloy and cross section.\n\nFor Overlap Type Wave Springs and multiple turn Spirawaves, the radial wall must be sufficient to prevent misalignment between adjacent layers. Its I.D. clears a shaft by .010 per side. As the spring is deflected, the O.D. and I.D. grow larger until the O.D. contacts the bore.         "text": "Conventional Gap and Overlap Type Wave Springs are used in a wide variety of applications. For short deflections and low-medium forces, they function with precision and dependability. These two types of Smalley Wave Springs permit radial expansion or growth in diameter within a cavity, without the binding or hang-up normally associated with die stamped wave washers. Just as their terms imply, the gap type is split to retain a gap between the ends; while the overlap type has overlapping ends. Thus, the ends are free to move circumferentially as the spring outside diameter grows during compression. For example, the O.D. of a Gap Type Wave Spring would fit .020 loose per side in a bore. Its I.D. clears a shaft by .010 per side. As the spring is deflected, the O.D. and I.D. grow larger until the O.D. contacts the bore.         "text": "There are 120, 100, 96, 84, 80, 72, 60, 54, and 48 slot cylinders ... the 80, 72, 60, and 54 are the most common; 120 is really rare! The cylinder sits inside the cam, and the needles ride up and down the slots of the cylinder to knit the socks.\n\nThe main thing about them is the number of slots -- we say \"this is a 72\", meaning the cylinder has 72 slots in it. The one shown here is a 72. There are 120, 100, 96, 84, 80, 72, 60, 54, and 48 slot cylinders ... the 80, 72, 60, and 54 are the most common; 120 is really rare! The cylinder sits inside the cam, and the needles ride up and down the slots of the cylinder to knit the socks. A bit like a geared, extra-slotted, knitting mushroom. For dimensions, most cylinders have a standard diameter (with small variances) of 4 1/2\u201d, and compound cylinders (rarer) have a working diameter of 3 1/2\u201d. Most Legare 400 and Autoknitter cylinders are interchangeable. The Legare 47 tends to have a slightly smaller cylinder size. Though, older machines can tend to fit only the cylinders that come with them, due to shifting in roundness or size or the hand-machining of them in the first place.\n\nSo it's best to take very close measurements if you buy a cylinder blind, unless the seller is a knowledgeable sock machine person themselves with the same machine brand and model (and series! I had 3 Legare 400's once obviously from different generations -- I was lucky though, they all swapped cylinders smoothly.) The number of slots controls the sock size (or, rather, number of needles in the slots). A 72 or 80 slot cylinder uses sock yarn like regia and opal to knit nice adult socks for pretty much any adult \u2013 adjust the tension looser for mr. giant feet, tighter for ms. normal foot. A 60 slot or 54 slot can take a slightly thicker yarn (I\u2019ve only tried up to DK weight \u2013 the needles tend to split thicker yarns, a real pain!) to knit an adult sock, or stick with sock yarn and a tight tension to knit kids\u2019 socks. The smallest sock I can knit on a 54 at the tightest tension it will reasonably knit fit my daughter\u2019s size 13 (she\u2019s 8 years old, so that\u2019s a kids 13) feet.\n\nThe compound cylinders are interesting; at the base they are 4 1/2\" in diameter, but they neck-down to 3 1/2\" at the top, and have needles with a very long tail-leg so the lifters in the cam can raise the needles. They are useful for toddler and baby socks, and really skinny scarves. There are also 100 and more slot cylinders, those are useful for very, very fine yarns. I have knit a tube on my 100, but that\u2019s all so far. there\u2019s a cone of zephyr yarn (merino/silk laceweight) in my stash waiting for it \u2026 someday! butt + 0.36 clear)\nBUTT_DEPTH       = 1.90       # mm radial (same as slot depth)\n\n# Drive hub interface (mates V1.3 drive hub: 18mm boss \u00d7 3mm tall)\nHUB_BOSS_OD      = 18.0       # V1.3 hub boss OD\nHUB_POCKET_D     = 18.15      # cylinder pocket - 0.15mm slip fit on boss\nHUB_POCKET_H     = 3.0        # depth of pocket\nHUB_POCKET_CHAM  = 0.5        # mm chamfer at pocket entry (assembly aid)\n\n# Bolt pattern (4\u00d7 M5 at 90\u00b0 spacing, securing cylinder to hub flange)\nBOLT_COUNT       = 4\nBOLT_PCD         = 70.0       # bolt circle diameter\nBOLT_HOLE_D      = 5.4        # M5 clearance hole\nBOLT_CB_D        = 9.5        # M5 socket head counterbore\nBOLT_CB_H        = 5.0        # counterbore depth\n\n# Outer chamfers\nEDGE_CHAMFER     = 0.6        # mm - top and bottom outer edges\n\n# Test wedge (30\u00b0 slice = 6 slots)\nWEDGE_ANGLE_DEG  = 30.0       # 6 slots \u00d7 5\u00b0 pitch (360/72)\nWEDGE_SLOT_WIDTHS = [1.20, 1.20, 1.22, 1.22, 1.25, 1.25]  # 3 width variants\n\n# =============================================================================\n# DERIVED VALUES\n# =============================================================================\n\nCYL_OUTER_R      = CYL_OD / 2.0\nCYL_INNER_R      = CYL_ID / 2.0\nSLOT_PITCH_DEG   = 360.0 / SLOT_COUNT          # 5.0 deg\nSLOT_PITCH_MM    = math.pi * CYL_OD / SLOT_COUNT  # 4.987 mm\nWALL_BETWEEN     = SLOT_PITCH_MM - SLOT_WIDTH    # 3.77mm\n\nprint(\"=\" * 70)\nprint(\"CSM V3 - CYLINDER V1.0 (Legare 4.5\\\", 72-slot)\")\nprint(\"=\" * 70)\nprint(f\"  Cylinder OD:        {CYL_OD}mm\")\nprint(f\"  Cylinder ID:        {CYL_ID}mm\")\nprint(f\"  Height:             {CYL_HEIGHT}mm\")\nprint(f\"  Slot count:         {SLOT_COUNT}\")\nprint(f\"  Slot pitch:         {SLOT_PITCH_DEG}deg / {SLOT_PITCH_MM:.3f}mm\")\nprint(f\"  Slot W x D:         {SLOT_WIDTH} x {SLOT_DEPTH}mm\")\nprint(f\"  Slot length:        {SLOT_LENGTH}mm axial\")\nprint(f\"  Wall between slots: {WALL_BETWEEN:.3f}mm\")\nprint(f\"  Butt cavity:        {BUTT_WIDTH} x {BUTT_HEIGHT}mm\")\nprint(f\"  Hub pocket:         D{HUB_POCKET_D} x {HUB_POCKET_H}mm\")\nprint(f\"  Bolt pattern:       {BOLT_COUNT}x M5 @ PCD {BOLT_PCD}mm\")\nprint()\n\n# =============================================================================\n# DOCUMENT\n# =============================================================================\ndoc = FreeCAD.newDocument(\"CSM_Cylinder_V1_0\")\n\n# =============================================================================\n# HELPER: Build a single slot solid\n# =============================================================================\n# Slot is a rectangular cut from outer surface, going RADIALLY inward.\n# Slot occupies the TOP zone of the cylinder (stem zone).\n# Below the slot, a butt cavity is cut (wider/shorter, axially).\n# Slot is positioned by angular index (0 to 71) and the BOTTOM-OF-SLOT Z height.\n\ndef build_slot_cutter(angle_deg, slot_width, slot_depth, slot_length,\n                      butt_width, butt_height, butt_depth,\n                      cyl_height, slot_chamfer):\n    \"\"\"\n    Build a cutter shape representing one slot + butt cavity at the given angle.\n    Returns a single Part shape ready to be cut from the cylinder.\n    \n    Geometry: oriented along +X axis initially, then rotated to angle_deg.\n    The cutter extends radially OUTWARD from cylinder center.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Slot top is at Z = cyl_height (top face)\n    # Slot bottom is at Z = cyl_height - slot_length\n    # Butt cavity below slot: Z = (cyl_height - slot_length) down to (cyl_height - slot_length - butt_height)\n    \n    slot_top_z    = cyl_height\n    slot_bot_z    = cyl_height - slot_length\n    butt_top_z    = slot_bot_z\n    butt_bot_z    = slot_bot_z - butt_height\n    \n    # Slot shape: thin rectangular box\n    # Place it so it cuts INTO the cylinder from outside\n    # Box dimensions: width (Y), depth (X going inward), length (Z)\n    # Position: centered at cylinder OD on +X axis, Y centered, Z spanning slot length\n    \n    # Slot box - extends from outer surface inward by slot_depth + safety margin\n    slot_x_outer = CYL_OUTER_R + 1.0   # 1mm beyond OD for clean cut\n    slot_x_inner = CYL_OUTER_R - slot_depth\n    slot_box = Part.makeBox(\n        slot_x_outer - slot_x_inner,  # X dimension (radial)\n        slot_width,                   # Y dimension (circumferential)\n        slot_length                   # Z dimension (axial)\n    )\n    # Box is created at origin, so translate to place it correctly\n    slot_box.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(slot_x_inner, -slot_width/2.0, slot_bot_z))\n    \n    # Butt cavity box - wider and taller than slot\n    butt_x_outer = CYL_OUTER_R + 1.0\n    butt_x_inner = CYL_OUTER_R - butt_depth\n    butt_box = Part.makeBox(\n        butt_x_outer - butt_x_inner,\n        butt_width,\n        butt_height\n    )\n    butt_box.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(butt_x_inner, -butt_width/2.0, butt_bot_z))\n    \n    # Lead-in chamfer at slot top (a small angled wedge above the slot opening)\n    # This is a small triangular prism at the slot's top edge\n    # Approximated by a slightly enlarged slot-top region\n    if slot_chamfer > 0.0:\n        cham_x_outer = CYL_OUTER_R + 1.0\n        cham_x_inner = CYL_OUTER_R - slot_chamfer  # shallow chamfer\n        cham_box = Part.makeBox(\n            cham_x_outer - cham_x_inner,\n            slot_width + 2 * slot_chamfer,    # wider at top\n            slot_chamfer + 0.1                # short chamfer height\n        )\n        cham_box.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(cham_x_inner,\n                                          -(slot_width + 2 * slot_chamfer) / 2.0,\n                                          slot_top_z - slot_chamfer))\n        cutter = slot_box.fuse(butt_box).fuse(cham_box)\n    else:\n        cutter = slot_box.fuse(butt_box)\n    \n    # Rotate cutter to the requested angle around Z axis\n    cutter.rotate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, 0),\n                  FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, 1),\n                  angle_deg)\n    \n    return cutter\n\n\n# =============================================================================\n# BUILD: FULL 72-SLOT CYLINDER\n# =============================================================================\nprint(\"\\n[1/2] Building FULL 72-slot cylinder...\")\n\n# Base cylinder shell (hollow tube)\nouter_cyl = Part.makeCylinder(CYL_OUTER_R, CYL_HEIGHT)\ninner_cyl = Part.makeCylinder(CYL_INNER_R, CYL_HEIGHT + 2)\ninner_cyl.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, -1))\ncyl_body = outer_cyl.cut(inner_cyl)\n\n# Hub pocket on bottom face\npocket = Part.makeCylinder(HUB_POCKET_D / 2.0, HUB_POCKET_H + 0.1)\npocket.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, -0.05))\ncyl_body = cyl_body.cut(pocket)\n\n# Hub pocket lead-in chamfer\nif HUB_POCKET_CHAM > 0:\n    cham_outer = Part.makeCone(\n        HUB_POCKET_D / 2.0 + HUB_POCKET_CHAM,\n        HUB_POCKET_D / 2.0,\n        HUB_POCKET_CHAM,\n    )\n    cham_outer.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, -0.001))\n    cyl_body = cyl_body.cut(cham_outer)\n\n# Bolt holes (4x M5 with counterbores)\nfor i in range(BOLT_COUNT):\n    angle = i * (360.0 / BOLT_COUNT)\n    rad = BOLT_PCD / 2.0\n    x = rad * math.cos(math.radians(angle))\n    y = rad * math.sin(math.radians(angle))\n    \n    # M5 clearance hole through full height\n    hole = Part.makeCylinder(BOLT_HOLE_D / 2.0, CYL_HEIGHT + 2)\n    hole.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(x, y, -1))\n    cyl_body = cyl_body.cut(hole)\n    \n    # Counterbore on bottom (M5 socket head)\n    cb = Part.makeCylinder(BOLT_CB_D / 2.0, BOLT_CB_H + 0.1)\n    cb.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(x, y, -0.05))\n    cyl_body = cyl_body.cut(cb)\n\n# 72 needle slots + butt cavities\nprint(\"  Cutting 72 slots...\")\nfor i in range(SLOT_COUNT):\n    angle = i * SLOT_PITCH_DEG\n    cutter = build_slot_cutter(\n        angle, SLOT_WIDTH, SLOT_DEPTH, SLOT_LENGTH,\n        BUTT_WIDTH, BUTT_HEIGHT, BUTT_DEPTH,\n        CYL_HEIGHT, SLOT_CHAMFER\n    )\n    cyl_body = cyl_body.cut(cutter)\n\n# Outer edge chamfers (top and bottom)\nif EDGE_CHAMFER > 0:\n    try:\n        edges_to_chamfer = []\n        bb = cyl_body.BoundBox\n        for e in cyl_body.Edges:\n            v1 = e.Vertexes[0].Point\n            v2 = e.Vertexes[1].Point\n            # Find horizontal circular edges at outer radius\n            if abs(v1.z - v2.z) < 0.01:  # horizontal edge\n                r1 = (v1.x ** 2 + v1.y ** 2) ** 0.5\n                # Only outermost edge (at OD), top and bottom faces only\n                if abs(r1 - CYL_OUTER_R) < 0.05:\n                    if abs(v1.z - 0) < 0.05 or abs(v1.z - CYL_HEIGHT) < 0.05:\n                        edges_to_chamfer.append(e)\n        if edges_to_chamfer:\n            cyl_body = cyl_body.makeChamfer(EDGE_CHAMFER, edges_to_chamfer)\n            print(f\"  Chamfered {len(edges_to_chamfer)} outer edges\")\n    except Exception as ex:\n        print(f\"  Outer chamfer skipped: {ex}\")\n\nobj_full = doc.addObject(\"Part::Feature\", \"Cylinder_V1_0_FULL\")\nobj_full.Shape = cyl_body\nobj_full.ViewObject.ShapeColor = (0.3, 0.5, 0.7)\nprint(f\"  Volume:  {cyl_body.Volume:.0f}mm^3\")\nprint(f\"  Surface: {cyl_body.Area:.0f}mm^2\")\n\n# =============================================================================\n# BUILD: 30 DEG TEST WEDGE\n# =============================================================================\nprint(\"\\n[2/2] Building 30 deg test wedge (6 slots, 3 width variants)...\")\n\n# Wedge is a 30-degree pie slice of the cylinder, with 6 slots\n# Slot widths: [1.20, 1.20, 1.22, 1.22, 1.25, 1.25] for empirical fit testing\n\n# Build full ring first\nwedge_outer = Part.makeCylinder(CYL_OUTER_R, CYL_HEIGHT)\nwedge_inner = Part.makeCylinder(CYL_INNER_R, CYL_HEIGHT + 2)\nwedge_inner.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, -1))\nwedge_body = wedge_outer.cut(wedge_inner)\n\n# Cut to 30-degree wedge: keep angles 0 to 30 deg\n# Build a \"keeping\" volume = 30deg sector + a bit of cylinder around\n# Easiest: subtract a 330-degree sector from the ring\n\n# Build a large pie slice covering 330 degrees (the part to remove)\n# We want to KEEP angles 0 to 30 degrees centered on slots\n# So slots should be at 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 deg... actually let's center the wedge\n# Wedge spans -2.5 to +27.5 deg, slots at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 deg\n\n# Simpler: build a sector to KEEP (a 30-deg pie slice) and intersect with the ring\nkeep_sector = Part.makeCylinder(CYL_OUTER_R + 5, CYL_HEIGHT + 2,\n                                FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, -1),\n                                FreeCAD.Vector(0, 0, 1),\n                                WEDGE_ANGLE_DEG)\n# This makes a partial cylinder spanning 0 to WEDGE_ANGLE_DEG degrees\n# Intersect with our hollow ring to get just the wedge\nwedge_body = wedge_body.common(keep_sector)\n\n# Cut 6 slots at angles 2.5, 7.5, 12.5, 17.5, 22.5, 27.5 deg (centered in wedge slots)\n# Each with its own width from WEDGE_SLOT_WIDTHS\nprint(\"  Cutting 6 test slots with widths:\", WEDGE_SLOT_WIDTHS)\nfor i, slot_w in enumerate(WEDGE_SLOT_WIDTHS):\n    angle = (i + 0.5) * SLOT_PITCH_DEG  # centers at 2.5, 7.5, etc.\n    cutter = build_slot_cutter(\n        angle, slot_w, SLOT_DEPTH, SLOT_LENGTH,\n        BUTT_WIDTH, BUTT_HEIGHT, BUTT_DEPTH,\n        CYL_HEIGHT, SLOT_CHAMFER\n    )\n    wedge_body = wedge_body.cut(cutter)\n\n# Position wedge offset from full cylinder for visualization\nwedge_body.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(150, 0, 0))\n\nobj_wedge = doc.addObject(\"Part::Feature\", \"Cylinder_V1_0_TESTWEDGE\")\nobj_wedge.Shape = wedge_body\nobj_wedge.ViewObject.ShapeColor = (0.7, 0.5, 0.3)\nprint(f\"  Volume:  {wedge_body.Volume:.0f}mm^3 (~{wedge_body.Volume * 1.27 / 1000:.1f}g PETG)\")\n\ndoc.recompute()\n\n# =============================================================================\n# EXPORT STLs\n# =============================================================================\nprint(\"\\nExporting STL files...\")\n\ntry:\n    # Full cylinder STL (centered at origin)\n    full_export = obj_full.Shape.copy()\n    tmp_full = doc.addObject(\"Part::Feature\", \"tmp_full\")\n    tmp_full.Shape = full_export\n    Part.export([tmp_full], PATH_STL_FULL)\n    doc.removeObject(\"tmp_full\")\n    print(f\"  [OK] FULL STL:  {PATH_STL_FULL}\")\n    \n    # Test wedge STL (translate back to origin for printing)\n    wedge_export = obj_wedge.Shape.copy()\n    wedge_export.translate(FreeCAD.Vector(-150, 0, 0))  # cancel +150 offset\n    tmp_wedge = doc.addObject(\"Part::Feature\", \"tmp_wedge\")\n    tmp_wedge.Shape = wedge_export\n {ex}\")\n\n# =============================================================================\n# EXPORT BLUEPRINT SVG (top view + side section)\n# }}\n    .body  {{ fill: #d4e1ed; stroke: #1e3a5f; stroke-width: 1.5; }}\n    .slot  {{ fill: #fff; stroke: #b91c1c; stroke-width: 0.5; }}\n    .ctr   {{ stroke: #888; stroke-dasharray: 4 2; See the row of images below for the Open CAM Legare (my machine), the Autoknitter and the Erlbacher machines. *Note Erlbacher has now dropped Gearhart from its name. They are now known as Erlbacher Knitting Machine. They began creating their new machines in the past inspired by the vintage Gearhart 1924 antique machines.\n\nI\u2019ve created two useful videos to dip your toe. The Legare (Closed Cam). The Autoknitter (Open Cam). Of all the components, most of the differences are the CAMs. A CAM is simply the metal bits on the inside of the machine shell that raise the needle into work. There are two basic CAM styles - Open or Closed. And with those CAM styles the dial that is turned to loosen or tighten the stitch created - the tension stitch dial - differs. See the image. ... Watch the Legare and Autoknitter videos on my website as they explain the CAMS while also introducing the machines themselves (most are very similar). Personally I prefer the CLOSED CAM machines because: -it can go in reverse without needing to lift needles so there\u2019s less likely an issue with jamming the cams \u00b7 -the tension dial on a OPEN CAM is one where the knob can be turned tighter or looser than the machine can actually knit (by design) making it more difficult for new users to find the right setting \u00b7\n\nSome machines with OPEN CAMs are: Erlbacher new machines, Autoknitters (including the newer NZAK Ultimate, Quiknit, and the vintage Gearhart machines). Some examples of machines with CLOSED CAMs are Legares (AKMC Automatic Knitting Machine Company, the Bi, Creelman Bros Banner Machine, Creelman Bros WorldStar, Caducque Rapide, the Cymbal, Griswold, Harrison Sun Circular, Imperia, Ideal, the Lama, L'Eclaire, La Perfection Bruxelles, Max Geltz, the Rekord, Sameuse, the Vega, the Wikuna). Want to see what those things are? See pictures of these cams at CSM Misc (Cams) Why am I mentioning CAMS? Closed CAM machines like the LEGARE allow you to go in reverse easily without having to lift any needles. Open CAM machine like those mentioned above, require a certain number of cylinder needles to be lifted in order to clear the CAMS of the cylinder needle butts (bottom foot area of each needle) - otherwise when changing directions they get sometimes hopelessly jammed.\n\nFurther differences on the OPEN CAM machines can sometimes be seen with their \u201cUpthrow Cams\u201d (teardrop shaped moving parts on the inside of the shell) where some machines have springs on those two parts (they are in pairs on each machine). An example of a machine with spring controlled Upthrow Cams is the new Erlbacher machines - springs translate into a much louder machine as each spring loaded upthrow cam hits a needle butt. However there are also other machines with those same Upthrow Cams without springs like the Autoknitter. There you have it. That\u2019s the main differences. See the row of images below for the Open CAM Legare (my machine), the Autoknitter and the Erlbacher machines. *Note Erlbacher has now dropped Gearhart from its name. They are now known as Erlbacher Knitting Machine. They began creating their new machines in the past inspired by the vintage Gearhart 1924 antique machines.\n\nPersonally I consider the LEGARE 400 (a vintage machine) to be better than the Autoknitters or vintage Gearharts - mostly due to smoothness of operation, ease to work on the machine without needing to lift needles when going in reverse and finally ease to get parts made from Chambord CSM - although this same supplier does make Autoknitter and other machine parts. Watch my unknitting video for why I love the Legare. HOWEVER there are many happy owners of Autoknitters, vintage Gearhart machines and other vintage European machines. The modern Erlbacher Gearhart machine is based off of the vintage 1924 Gearhart machine, the modern machine is now on its second ribber version. The Autoknitter crankwheel is often pictured with more than four hole cutouts to help visually tell the two crankwheel a apart. The vintage Gearhart crank has 50 teeth, an Auto Knitter has 72. Some old Creelman machines have a mount that could use both cranks. The Autoknitter cylinders WILL NOT fit a LEGARE unless the different cylinder screw hole alignment holes are added to accommodate the different screw mount locations on the Bed Plate. Also the ribber attachment hole on an Autoknitter cylinder is in the wrong location for a Legare machine. Autoknitter dials WILL fit a Legare IF you have an Ribber Post Adapter as the holes are different on the Ribber Dial. Ribber Post Adapters hold the Ribber Dial and Tappet onto the Ribber Arm by means of a screw.\n\nSome machines have numbers stamped on the baseplate near the vertical yarn mast, some have no numbers at all, while still others have numbers stamped onto the top edge of the cam shell. Further to that, some Tension Dials have a number posted beneath the dial - one person said it was to note the thread of the screw holes in that component for later identification for machine assembling purposes. The creelman manual available online for this closed cam machine indicate this machine was made with one of two V Cam styles (the autoknitter open Cam being built with one of three V Cam styles).\n\nHaving issues trying to get a successful needle to yarn alignment with the Yarn Carrier? You may need to adjust the Yarn Carrier Timing if you have a newer machine like mine. The newer version has two YARN CARRIER TIMING BOLTS WITH NUT on the COG RING (the COG RING is the flat round part that connects with the crankwheel to move the machine in either direction). Putting it simply, if you have the two adjuster bolts on the cog wheel (over a non-adjustable nob of metal of the older version) it allows you to lengthen or shorten the distance to the cam shell contact thus adjusting the wave of the stitch. One bolt adjusts forward knitting (counter clockwise) the other bolt adjusts reverse knitting (clockwise). If the Yarn Carrier Timing is off you might not be having the wave of successful needle action at the right point. Cam ring decision\n\nI want to keep V6 cam ring **single-profile** (one knit point per rotation). The reason:\n\n- Multi-cam profiles (one cam set per feeder) is much more complex\n- Time to knit is inversely proportional to number of feeders\n- For DIY, single cam + sequential feeder activation is simpler and works well\n\n**Trade-off:** With 1 cam profile, 6 feeders means yarn switching happens at one rotation point, not 6 simultaneous knit points. =============================================================================\n# CAM PROFILE FUNCTION\n# =============================================================================\n\ndef cam_z_bot(theta_deg):\n    \"\"\"Returns Z bottom of cam slot at given angle (in degrees).\"\"\"\n    if theta_deg < ANGLE_RISE_START:\n        return Z_REST\n    elif theta_deg < ANGLE_RISE_END:\n Functional equivalence for our geometry:\n   The needle butt is anchored to a rotating cylinder. It cannot\n   move radially outward beyond the cylinder OD. Both my \"shorter ceiling\"\n   and a \"true overhang\" constrain Z motion at the same height.\n   The radial-overhang advantage applies to designs where the butt\n   could escape radially - not ours.\n\n2. Implementation simplicity:\n   Shorter ceiling = simple cylindrical cut, easy to print.\n   True overhang = complex geometry with concave feature, harder to\n   print on FDM (would need supports or fail).\n\n3. Recovery path:\n   If post-test results show the shorter ceiling isn't enough,\n   V7 can implement true overhang.
